A sponsored immigrant is an individual who is legally admitted to Canada under a sponsorship agreement. A sponsor is an individual who meets the Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) requirements and has agreed to financially support the sponsored immigrant while they live in Canada. The sponsor is responsible for supporting the sponsored immigrant for the duration of the sponsorship agreement which is also known as the undertaking period. Under a sponsorship agreement, the sponsor and the sponsored immigrant both agree to certain responsibilities for the duration of the undertaking period. The sponsor agrees to provide basic needs (e.g. food, clothing, shelter) to the sponsored immigrant and the sponsored immigrant agrees to make every effort to support themselves and their accompanying family members. Even if a sponsored immigrant obtains Canadian citizenship, their sponsorship agreement is in effect for the duration of the undertaking or until there is a sponsorship breakdown. For more information, Sponsorship Agreement (Policy) Sponsorship categories and undertakings The undertaking period starts on the day the sponsored immigrant becomes a permanent resident. The category and the length of the undertaking depend on: the sponsored immigrant's age; the sponsored immigrant's relationship to the sponsor; and where the sponsorship agreement was signed.

A sponsored immigrant is an individual who has been admitted to Canada as a permanent resident under a sponsorship agreement. The Sponsorship evidence is used to record whether a client entered Canada under a sponsorship agreement. This evidence is not read by Eligibility and Entitlement rules. The Sponsorship Agreement evidence is used to record the details of the sponsorship period. This is the evidence used by the Eligibility and Entitlement rules. The Sponsorship and Sponsorship Agreement evidences exist in both Application Cases and Integrated Cases. If the pension or benefit is not approved, the evidences are maintained in the Application Case. If the pension or benefit is authorized and approved, the evidences are maintained in the Integrated Case. The sponsorship information provided by the client must be validated. Refer to Validate Sponsorship Agreement and Breakdown Details (Action) . Once the sponsorship information has been validated and the required documentation has been received, if applicable, the Sponsorship Agreement evidence must be added or updated. Validate Sponsorship Agreement and Breakdown Details (Action) If the Sponsorship and the Sponsorship Agreement evidences were added to an Integrated Case, they must be activated. If the evidences were added to an Application Case, the evidence will be active automatically.

Sponsorship agreements restrict entitlement to income-tested benefits, but they do not affect eligibility. An applicant is not entitled to an income-tested benefit if they are a sponsored immigrant. However, an application for an income-tested benefit cannot be denied for that reason. The ALW benefit must not be paid to the spouse or common-law partner of a pensioner for any period during which the pensioner is not entitled to the GIS because they are under a sponsorship agreement. For more information, Eligibility Requirements— ALW Benefit New Business (Policy) Grandfathering rules In January 2014, amendments were made to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) regulations to increase the undertaking length for Parents and Grandparents (PGP) sponsorship agreements from 10 years to 20 years. Although the amendments came into force in January 2014, sponsored immigrants did not begin entering Canada under the 20-year PGP sponsorship agreements until approximately January 2016. In October 2025, amendments made to the Old Age Security Act (OAS Act) came into force, limiting entitlement to income-tested benefits for sponsored immigrants for the duration of their sponsorship, regardless of their years of Canadian residence. If the income-tested benefit effective date is: October 1, 2025 or later, applicants will be subject to the new OAS Act amendments. Prior to October 1, 2025, the benefit will be assessed using the previous entitlement criteria for sponsored immigrants, regardless of when the application is received. Benefit effective date is October 1, 2025 or later If the effective date of the income-tested benefit is October 1, 2025 or later, a sponsored immigrant is not entitled to the benefit for the entire duration of the sponsorship agreement, unless there is a sponsorship breakdown. If all other eligibility requirements are met, sponsored immigrants are entitled to receive income-tested benefits in the earlier of: the month that a sponsorship breakdown occurs; or the month after the sponsorship agreement ends. Benefit effective date is prior to October 1, 2025 If the effective date of the income-tested benefit is prior to October 1, 2025, a sponsored immigrant is not entitled to receive any income-tested benefit for the entire duration of the sponsorship agreement, unless: there is a sponsorship breakdown; or the sponsored immigrant accumulates 10 full years of residence in Canada after the age of 18. If all other eligibility requirements are met, sponsored immigrants are entitled to receive income-tested benefits in the earlier of: the month that a sponsorship breakdown occurs; the month after they accumulate 10 years of residence in Canada after the age of 18; or the month after the sponsorship agreement ends. For more information, Sponsorship Agreement (Policy) Sponsorship evidence in Cúram When an Application Case for an income-tested benefit is authorized and the applicant's Sponsorship Agreement evidence is added in Cúram, the applicant will be eligible but not entitled. The system will not calculate any entitlement for the duration of the sponsorship agreement unless: there is a sponsorship breakdown; or the benefit's effective date was prior to October 2025 and the applicant has accumulated 10 years of Canadian residence before their sponsorship end date. When an Application Case for an ALW benefit is authorized and the Sponsorship Agreement evidence for the spouse or common-law partner is added in Cúram, the system will not calculate any entitlement for the duration of the spouse or common-law partner's sponsorship agreement unless: there is a sponsorship breakdown; or the spouse or common-law partner's GIS effective date was prior to October 2025 and they have accumulated 10 years of Canadian residence before their sponsorship end date.

Entitlement to the GIS is based on: marital status; and individual income or the combined net income of the applicant and their spouse or common-law partner, for the preceding calendar year. A GIS application must be approved if the applicant has met the eligibility criteria. However, there will be situations where an application is approved with no entitlement. An application will be approved with no entitlement when: the applicant is a sponsored immigrant at the effective date; the individual income or the combined income of the applicant and their spouse or common-law partner is in excess; or the applicant is incarcerated. An application will be approved but the entitlement cannot be determined in situations when: eligibility has been met; and required information or documentation has not been received to determine the entitlement amount (e.g. clarification of their or their spouse or common-law partner's income, documentation required to confirm foreign pension, documentation to confirm sponsorship agreement details).

Entitlement to an ALW benefit is based on the combined net income of the OAS pensioner and the ALW benefit applicant. An ALW benefit application must be approved if the applicant has met the eligibility criteria. However, there will be situations where an application is approved with no entitlement to the benefit. An application is approved with no entitlement when: the applicant is a sponsored immigrant at the effective date; the applicant has a spouse or common-law partner who is eligible to the GIS but not entitled to it as they are a sponsored immigrant; the combined income of the applicant and their spouse or common-law partner is in excess; or the applicant is incarcerated. An application will be approved but entitlement to the benefit cannot be determined in situations when: eligibility has been met; and required information or documentation has not been received to determine the entitlement amount (e.g. clarification of their or their spouse or common-law partner's income, documentation required to confirm foreign pension, documentation to confirm sponsorship agreement details).

Eligibility requirements To approve an ALW application, all of the following requirements must be met: an application must be received, and it must include: the applicant's signature; and confirmation of the applicant's eligibility based on their age, residence, legal status and marital status (e.g. married or in a common-law relationship with a GIS pensioner who is eligible for the GIS); and a statement of income from the applicant. Entitlement requirements To determine entitlement, the following are required: a statement of income from the applicant's spouse or common-law partner; and the spouse or common-law partner's signature. A signature confirms they are the spouse or common-law partner of the applicant and that the information provided is valid. It also provides their consent for the Department to request their statement of income from the CRA, if required. Under the Old Age Security Act , the spouse or common-law partner is responsible for providing their statement of income and signature. If the applicant or the spouse or common-law partner provides their signature on the application or statement of income form, but the income information field is blank, the Department can request their income information from the CRA. If the CRA does not have their income as they did not file their taxes, the applicant or the spouse or common-law partner must provide their income information. The applicant is eligible but not entitled for the ALW and the application is approved If an individual applies for the ALW benefit and meets the legislative eligibility requirements for the ALW , but their spouse or common-law partner does not provide their statement of income or signature, the application can be approved, but the entitlement cannot be determined until the spouse or common-law partner provides their statement of income and signature. The ALW benefit application can be approved with no entitlement if the individual meets the eligibility requirements for the ALW , but they are not entitled if: they are under a sponsorship agreement; they are incarcerated; the GIS pensioner is eligible for the GIS but not entitled as they are under a sponsorship agreement; or the GIS pensioner is eligible for the GIS but not entitled as the couple's combined income is in excess. Exceptions: There are exceptions where the ALW applicant can still meet the entitlement requirements for the ALW even though the pensioner is not entitled to the GIS. The exceptions include: when the pensioner is incarcerated; and when the pensioner is entitled to the GIS but chooses not to receive it. The applicant is not eligible for the ALW benefit and the application is denied If the applicant does not meet the required eligibility requirements, the application must be denied and the individual informed of their reconsideration rights.

Amendments to the Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada’s regulations came into force in January 2014 and individuals began entering Canada under a 20-year Parents and Grandparents (PGP) sponsorship agreement around January 2016. Since it is expected that most 10-year sponsorship agreements will have lapsed by the time the amendments to the Old Age Security Act come into force, grandfathering rules will apply under limited situations. Effective date is before October 1, 2025 Individuals under a sponsorship agreement who submit an application with an effective date before October 1, 2025, will continue to be assessed under the old rules, even if the application is received after this date. Old Rules Individuals under a 10-year PGP sponsorship agreement with an effective date prior to October 1, 2025, who have not yet applied for benefits, will be subjected to the old rules even if their sponsorship agreement has not yet ended. Under the old rules, sponsored immigrants are not entitled to receive the GIS, ALW benefit or ALWS benefit for the duration of their sponsorship agreement. The limitation on entitlement remains in effect until: the beneficiary accumulates 10 full years of residence in Canada after age 18; the sponsorship agreement ends; or the sponsorship agreement breaks down. Effective date is on or after October 1, 2025 Individuals under a sponsorship agreement who submit an application with an effective date on or after October 1, 2025 will be assessed under the new rule, regardless of the length of their sponsorship agreement. The rule being that an individual under a sponsorship agreement is not entitled to receive the GIS, ALW benefit or ALWS benefit for the duration of their sponsorship period.

A sponsored immigrant is an individual who is legally admitted to Canada under a sponsorship agreement. A sponsor is a Canadian citizen or permanent resident who is 18 years of age or older and has agreed to financially support the sponsored immigrant while living in Canada for the duration of the sponsorship period. Effective October 1, 2025, individuals under a sponsorship agreement are not entitled to receive the GIS, ALW benefit or ALWS benefit for the duration of their sponsorship period. Additionally, the duration of the Parents and Grandparents (PGP) sponsorship period has been extended from 10-years to 20-years in all provinces and territories except Quebec. This limitation on entitlement remains in effect until: the sponsorship agreement ends; or the sponsorship agreement breaks down. Once the sponsorship agreement ends or breaks down, the sponsored individual is entitled to receive the GIS, ALW benefit or ALWS benefit in the same manner as a non-sponsored immigrant.

An individual that is under a sponsorship undertaking is not entitled to receive a GIS, ALW or ALWS benefit for the duration of their sponsorship, or until they have obtained 10 years of residence in Canada, whichever comes first. When an applicant is unable to provide official documentation to confirm the sponsorship details needed to determine entitlement to one of these benefits, they can complete and sign the ISP3210 form. Once the form has been submitted to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) and they have located the applicant's record based on the information provided on the ISP3210 form, the details related to the applicant's sponsorship will be provided on the Verification of Status form.

In January 2014, changes were made to the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations . This increased the length of the Parents and Grandparents (PGP) sponsorship agreement period from 10 years to 20 years, which affects all provinces and territories except Québec. To align the OAS program with these changes, the Old Age Security Act (OAS Act) was amended in 2014 to limit the payment of income-tested benefits (i.e. GIS, ALW benefit and ALWS benefit). This limited the payment to sponsored individuals for the entire period of their sponsorship agreement, regardless of the type of sponsorship agreement or their years of residence. Individuals began entering Canada (in all provinces and territories except for Québec) under a 20-year PGP sponsorship agreement around January 2016. This means that the OAS Act amendments will begin impacting these individuals in 2026 when they attain 10 years of residence in Canada. Effective October 1, 2025, these amendments came into force through an Order in Council. This will affect income-tested benefit applications with an effective date on or after October 1, 2025. Sponsored individuals who are eligible for income-tested benefits with an effective date prior to October 1, 2025, will be grandfathered using the old sponsorship agreement rules.

In January 2014, changes were made to the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations which increased the length of the Parent and Grandparents (PGP) sponsorship period from 10 years to 20 years, affecting all provinces except Quebec. For individuals who landed in Quebec, the sponsorship period remains at 10 years, regardless of where they live in Canada now. Around January 2016, individuals began landing in Canada under 20-year PGP sponsorship agreements (except in Quebec). However, for a period of time after January 2016, some individuals still landed in Canada under 10-year PGP sponsorship agreements. Effective October 1, 2025, sponsored individuals will not be entitled to receive income-tested benefits for the entire period of their sponsorship agreement, regardless of the type or length of sponsorship agreement. Income-tested benefits with an effective date before October 1, 2025, will be grandfathered and processed under the old sponsorship agreement rules even if the application is received after this date. The interim guidance in this procedure must be followed until the updated policy, procedures and related forms and letters are published. Applications affected by the new sponsorship agreement rules must be placed on hold until an announcement is published to advise that all affected policy and procedures have been updated. When an application for income-tested benefits is received, you must determine if the applicant is under a sponsorship agreement, if the following conditions apply: The applicant was not born in Canada; The effective date of the initial income-tested benefit is October 1, 2025, or later; and The applicant has less than 20 years of residence in Canada from the date they became a permanent resident. If the application form does not allow for the applicant to provide this information or the applicant does not answer the sponsorship agreement question, and there is no supporting documentation on the file to confirm the sponsorship agreement, you must request it by phone or mail. The following sponsorship agreement details must be requested: The category of the sponsorship agreement; If the sponsorship agreement was with the province of Quebec; The length of the sponsorship agreement in months or years; The date the applicant became a permanent resident in Canada; and The applicant's Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) Unique Client Identifier (UCI) number. The applicant may not be able to provide all of the above information; however, they must provide enough information for you to confirm whether they are under a sponsorship agreement and the length of the sponsorship. All of the required information can be obtained over the phone, and a note must be added in ITRDS to record the sponsorship agreement details. Documentation Documentation to support the sponsorship agreement details may not be required; however, the Department can request it at any time. Some documents supporting an applicant’s legal status may include the sponsorship agreement details. Review the sponsorship agreement details provided by the applicant and any immigration documentation regarding the sponsorship agreement to ensure there are no discrepancies or situations that require confirmation, such as: The applicant indicated that they did not enter Canada under a sponsorship agreement. However, identifiers exist on any IRCC records that suggest a sponsorship undertaking (e.g. "FC" (Family Class) notations, completion of any fields related to sponsorship). The applicant’s permanent resident date is in January 2016 or later, and they indicate they are under a 10-year sponsorship agreement (except where they landed in Quebec). Although this situation may not be a discrepancy, it requires documentation before it is accepted. There is a discrepancy between the application and previously submitted information (e.g. a duplicate or previous application, documentation). If there is a discrepancy or situation that requires confirmation, request supporting documentation to confirm the sponsorship agreement details. Acceptable documentary evidence The following documents can be accepted to support the sponsorship agreement details: Confirmation from IRCC; Confirmation of Permanent Residence (IMM 5292) (older version); Confirmation of Permanent Residence (IMM 5688); Verification of Status (VOS) or replacement of Immigration Document (IMM 5716); Record of Landing (IMM 1000); Verification of Landing (IMM5617); Any official immigration documents that confirm the details of the sponsorship agreement; and Formulaire Demande d’engagement (A-0546-GF).

In January 2014, changes were made to the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations which increased the length of the parent and grandparent (PGP) sponsorship agreement period from 10 years to 20 years, affecting all provinces except Quebec. To align the OAS program with these changes, the OAS Act was amended in 2014 to limit the payment of income-tested benefits (i.e. GIS, ALW benefit and ALWS benefit) to sponsored individuals for the entire length of their sponsorship agreement, regardless of the type of sponsorship agreement or their years of residence in Canada. However, these amendments were not immediately brought into force. Individuals began landing in Canada (in all provinces except for Quebec) under 20-year parent and grandparent (PGP) sponsorship undertakings around January 2016. This means that the OAS Act amendments will begin impacting these individuals in 2026, when they will have attained 10 years of residence in Canada. These amendments will be brought into force through an Order in Council effective October 1, 2025, affecting income-tested benefit applications with an effective date of October 2025 or later. Sponsored individuals who are eligible for income-tested benefits with an effective date prior to October 2025 will be grandfathered using the old sponsorship agreement rules.

A sponsored immigrant may be entitled to income-tested benefits (i.e. GIS, ALW benefit, ALWS benefit) before the end date of their sponsorship agreement if there is a sponsorship breakdown. A sponsorship breakdown will occur if the sponsor: dies; is convicted of an offence under the Criminal Code in respect of the sponsored immigrant; becomes bankrupt; or is sentenced to a term of imprisonment of more than 6 months. In any of these situations, a sponsored immigrant could be entitled to income-tested benefits in the month of the sponsorship breakdown if all other eligibility requirements are met and the required income is received. For more information, Sponsorship Agreement (Policy) In all cases, documentary evidence is required to validate a sponsorship breakdown. For more information, Documentary Evidence—Sponsorship Agreements (Policy)

Income-tested benefits may be paid to sponsored individuals before the end of their sponsorship agreement only in the event of a sponsorship breakdown. The following conditions may qualify as a sponsorship breakdown: the sponsor dies; the sponsor is convicted of an offence under the Criminal Code in respect of the sponsored individual; the sponsor is determined to be bankrupt as defined in section 2 of the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act. ; or the sponsor is sentenced to a term of imprisonment of more than 6 months. For more information, Documentary Evidence - Sponsorship Agreements (Policy)

An applicant may qualify under the 10-year rule if: on July 1, 1977, they were 25 years of age or over; and resided in Canada or , if they did not reside in Canada: they resided in Canada after the age of 18; or they possessed a valid Canadian Immigration Visa; and they had resided in Canada for the 10 years immediately preceding the day of approval of their application (10-year period).
An applicant may qualify for a full OAS pension if they have accumulated 40 years of Canadian residence after their 18th birthday.

An individual may qualify for a full OAS pension under the 40-Year Rule, the 10-Year Rule or the 3 for 1 Rule. 40-Year Rule An individual can qualify for a full OAS pension by accumulating 40 years of residence in Canada after age 18. When all periods of residence in Canada after age 18 have been counted and they do not total 40 years, applicants may still be able to qualify for the full OAS pension under the 10-Year Rule or the 3 for 1 Rule, or they may reside in Canada for the additional period required for a full pension. 10-Year Rule An individual can qualify for a full OAS pension based on as little as 10 years of residence in Canada accumulated after age 18. The following situations describe the eligibility requirements that allow an applicant who has reached age 65 to qualify for a full OAS pension under the 10-Year Rule: On July 1, 1977 , the applicant was 25 years of age or older, was a resident of Canada and resided in Canada for the 10 years immediately preceding the day that their application is approved. On July 1, 1977 , the applicant was 25 years of age or older but was not a resident of Canada. They did however, reside in Canada for any period of time after age 18 and prior to July 1, 1977 , and resided in Canada for the 10 years immediately preceding the day that their application is approved. On July 1, 1977 , the applicant was 25 years of age or older but had no residence in Canada on or before that date. They did however, possess a valid immigration visa on or before July 1, 1977 and resided in Canada for the 10 years immediately preceding the day that their application is approved. Determining the 10-year period immediately before the date of approval of the application The day on which the application is approved is normally the applicant's 65th birthday. This means that applicants must have resided in Canada for the 10 years immediately preceding their 65th birthday to be eligible for payment of the pension to begin effective the following month. In the case of applicants who cannot fulfill the residence requirements when they reach age 65, their application is approved the day after they meet the 10-year period of residence in Canada. Where there have been absences from Canada in the 10-year period, the nature and duration of each one must be evaluated to determine whether the applicant remained a resident of Canada during the absence. If residence has been interrupted during the 10-year period, the application must be considered under the 3 for 1 Rule. 3 for 1 Rule When residence during the 10-year period has been interrupted by absences, it is still possible for an individual to qualify for a full OAS pension using the 3 for 1 Rule. This allows the applicant to make up for absences during the 10-year period by substituting, on a 3 for 1 basis, prior periods of time in Canada. The eligibility requirements to qualify for a full OAS pension are the same under the 3 for 1 and 10-Year Rules, with the exception of the following: The applicant does not have to have been a resident of Canada for a continuous period of 10 years immediately before the approval of the application. They can have absences during the 10-year period, provided that they are supplemented by prior time in Canada equal to at least 3 times the periods of the absences in the 10-year period. Any time spent in Canada after the applicant has reached age 18 and before the 10-year period (whether the applicant was a resident or present in Canada) can be used to make up for absences in the 10-year period. The applicant must be a resident of Canada for a continuous period of at least one year immediately before the day the application is approved. If there has not been a lengthy presence in Canada after age 18 and before the 10-year period, applicants may not be able to satisfy the residence requirements at the time of their 65th birthday or when submitting their application, whichever is later. It must then be determined on what date they will have sufficient make-up time to qualify, assuming that up to the date of approval, they will have no absences that interrupt residence in Canada. Once the effective date for a full OAS pension under the 3 for 1 Rule is calculated, applicants are informed of the earliest date on which they may qualify. They must also be informed that the calculation was made on the assumption that they would have no absences that would interrupt their residence in Canada up to that date and that any absences must be reported to the Department. When applicants applying from outside of Canada must return to Canada for one year to qualify under the 3 for 1 Rule, they are considered to have completed their year of residence on the day before the anniversary of the date on which the period of residence began.

For OAS pension and GIS automatic enrolment and the ALW benefit application, consider the following: An individual selected for OAS pension and GIS automatic enrolment may apply separately for the ALW benefit. Since there is no automatic enrolment for the ALW benefit, the individual must prove that they meet the eligibility criteria for the ALW benefit in the usual manner and with the relevant documentation. The selection criteria for the OAS pension and GIS automatic enrolment process cannot be used to approve the ALW benefit before age 65. The eligibility criteria are not proven until the OAS pension and GIS application are waived and the applicant is approved for the OAS pension and GIS. The ALW benefit application cannot be held until the applicant's 65th birthday because there is no legislative authority to hold it. ALW benefit applications must be processed in a timely manner.

For OAS pension and GIS automatic enrolment and the ALWS benefit application, consider the following: An individual selected for OAS pension and GIS automatic enrolment may apply separately for the ALWS benefit. Since there is no automatic enrolment for the ALWS benefit, the individual must prove that they meet the eligibility criteria for the ALWS benefit in the usual manner and with the relevant documentation. The selection criteria for the OAS pension and GIS automatic enrolment process cannot be used to approve the ALWS benefit before age 65. The eligibility criteria cannot be applied until the OAS pension and GIS application are waived and the individual is approved for the OAS pension and GIS. An ALWS benefit application cannot be held until the applicant's 65th birthday because there is no legislative authority to hold it. ALWS benefit applications must be processed in a timely manner.

Up until their 65th birthday, a selected client may opt-out of the automatic enrolment process for: the OAS pension and the GIS at the same time; the GIS alone; or the OAS pension alone after they have already opted-out of the GIS. By choosing to opt-out of the automatic enrolment of the OAS pension, the client is also choosing to opt-out of the automatic enrolment of the GIS. However, the client may opt-out of the automatic enrolment of the GIS only and continue with the automatic enrolment of the OAS pension. If the selected client continues to be eligible on the day of their 65th birthday, the requirement to submit an application is considered to have been waived and the OAS pension and the GIS, if applicable, have been authorized. Therefore, a request to opt-out of the automatic enrolment process must be received before the day of their 65th birthday in order to be considered valid. A selected client can opt-out of the automatic enrolment process by: requesting to opt-out on their Client Portal through their My Service Canada Account (MSCA); sending a letter to the Department requesting to opt-out of the automatic enrolment process of one or both benefits; returning the notification letter to the Department with a note (separate or made directly on the notification letter) requesting to opt-out of the automatic enrolment process of one or both benefits; or submitting an Application for the Old Age Security Pension and the Guaranteed Income Supplement (ISP-3550) form where the following criteria are met: the applicant indicated that they do not want to apply for the GIS (i.e. they checked the box in question C1); the applicant has not responded to any of the questions in Section C (i.e. questions C2 to C11); and you have obtained confirmation from the applicant by phone or mail that they wish to opt-out of the automatic enrolment process for the GIS. Refer to Request Documentation or Information by Phone or Mail (Action) . Request Documentation or Information by Phone or Mail (Action) If the selected client requests to opt-out of the automatic enrolment process through their Client Portal, Cúram will automatically process the request. All other requests will require manual processing in Cúram before the client’s 65th birthday to ensure that the Application Case is closed. The received date of the notification of the person's intention to opt-out is: the date of the MSCA opt-out transaction. This date is populated in the Withdrawal Date field of the Application Details evidence in the Application Case; or the date the Department received the incoming correspondence. If the client is excluded from the automatic enrolment process and wishes to receive the OAS pension and the GIS in the future, they must submit an application. The OAS Act allows the Minister to waive the requirement for an OAS pension and an initial GIS application if the ALW or ALWS benefit ceases to be payable when the beneficiary reaches the age of 65. For the purpose of the OAS Act, "payable" means the beneficiary is "eligible to receive a benefit" as opposed to being "entitled to (in receipt of) a benefit". When an ALW or ALWS beneficiary who has a lifetime renewal designation reaches age 65, using the information on file, it is possible to determine whether an OAS/GIS application is necessary to convert their account to an OAS/GIS based on whether they continue to meet all the eligibility requirements and entitlement.
Old Age Security Act Section 21(5.1)—Payment of allowance to survivors, Waiver of requirement for application

The Old Age Security Act allows the requirement for an initial Allowance for the Survivor (ALWS) application to be waived if the Allowance (ALW) would have been or was payable for the month in which the OAS pensioner spouse or common-law partner died. A separate application for the ALWS is not required. The ALW application is used and the ALW benefit is automatically converted to ALWS. For the purposes of the OAS Act, "Payable" means the beneficiary is "eligible to receive a benefit" as opposed to "being entitled to (in receipt of) a benefit". The Minister retains the right to solicit in certain circumstances where: residence or marital status requires verification; or an income tax return has not been filed for a number of years.

Automatic enrolment for the OAS pension Automatic enrolment for a full OAS pension allows the Minister to waive the requirement for an application at the age of 65 based on available information. The application is only waived if the Minister is satisfied that an individual is presumed to have met all of the eligibility requirements (age, residence and legal status) in the absence of evidence to the contrary. The Minister retains the right to cancel the automatic enrolment process and to request an application before the individual's 65th birthday. The Minister may also request documentary evidence (e.g. proof of age, residence or legal status) at any time before or after the approval of the OAS pension. OAS pension applications that meet the data elements to be automatically enrolled Individuals who submit a paper or online application to apply for a full OAS pension and who meet all the data elements to substantiate eligibility may have their eligibility to the OAS pension determined using the same rules and information. Automatic enrolment of the GIS Automatic enrolment for the GIS allows the Minister to waive the requirement for a GIS application at the age of 65 based on information that is made available. The application can only be waived if the Minister is satisfied, based on the information collected, that an individual meets the eligibility and entitlement criteria for the benefit. The Minister retains the right to cancel the automatic enrolment process and to request an application before the individual's 65th birthday. Individuals who are selected for the automatic enrolment of the OAS pension (Categories 1 and 2) will be screened for GIS automatic enrolment. In order to waive the requirement for a GIS application, the Minister must: be able to obtain a statement of income from the CRA; and determine the marital status of an individual and the identity of the spouse or common-law partner, if applicable, by leveraging existing data from the CRA and within the Department. The Department will obtain income and marital status information from the CRA to determine entitlement to the GIS. In order to waive the requirement for a GIS application, the selection of individuals for the GIS automatic enrolment can only occur if, at age 64 + 9 months, these individuals are single, widowed, divorced or separated and, for those individuals who are married or in a common-law relationship, their spouse or common-law partner's identity and information are already known to the Department.

When the estimated income is calculated, only pension income, employment income, and self-employment income are included. Income and deductions from all other sources from the actual income reported in the base calendar year is combined with the estimated income. This combined total option income is used to calculate entitlement. Refer to Options (Policy) for more information regarding the income to include in an option calculation. Options (Policy) If the base calendar year income is not available at the time of the option calculation, defer the Estimated Income 3041 task in Cúram until you receive the income information to determine the income-tested benefit entitlement for the period affected by the option. If the required income is not received after the appropriate bring forward periods, stop review of the option. Add an Is not entitled override to the income-tested benefit in the system for the current payment period to prevent Cúram from automatically calculating entitlement when the income is received. Once the required income is received, a task will be generated to review the account and determine entitlement for the base calendar year. Once the entitlement for the base calendar year has been determined, the option can be processed. If the client’s base calendar year income is received too late and they are not entitled to income-tested benefits for the period affected by the option, they are not entitled to the option for this period either. Special income considerations When you are reviewing and processing an ISP-3041 form, the following income types have special considerations: Seasonal Work; CPP/QPP Pension Sharing; CPP/QPP Credit Splitting; PRB ; PRB CPP/QPP lump sum payments ; CPP/QPP lump sum payments CPP/QPP Enhancement ; CPP/QPP Enhancement Wage Loss Replacement Income; Child or Spousal Support Payments; Pension Split Income ; Pension Split Income Foreign Pension Income; Pension Income Unduly Received ; Pension Income Unduly Received Provincial workers' compensation benefits (e.g. La Commission des normes de l'équité de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) in Quebec, Workplace Safety Insurance Board (WSIB) in Ontario); La Commission des normes de l'équité de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) Employment Insurance (EI) Benefits; Employment Insurance COVID-19 Emergency Benefits ; COVID-19 Emergency Benefits Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP) Income; Registered Retirement Income Fund (RRIF) Income (including transfers from a RRSP); Registered Retirement Income Fund (RRIF) Income Lump Sum Pension Income ; and Lump Sum Pension Income Option Following the Retirement of Fishing Licences. For more information regarding these special considerations, Options (Policy) PRB When you are reviewing income and see that a PRB is in pay, you must ensure that the individual has included this amount in their CPP or QPP monthly rate. The receipt of PRB retroactive payments is generally not an optionable event, unless the lump sum payment includes income for the previous year and the notional tax provision does not apply. Refer to Options—Post-Retirement Benefit (Action) to determine if the lump sum payment can be considered an optionable event and how to ensure the correct rate is used in the estimate when the income must be included in the estimate calculation. Options—Post-Retirement Benefit (Action) CPP/QPP lump sum payments A record of earnings (ROE) update or a delay in processing a pension or benefit can result in a retroactive lump sum payment. If the CPP or QPP lump sum is a retroactive payment that includes entitlement for a previous year and the amount is not considered under the Notional Tax Provision (i.e. less than $300.00 of the underpayment extends to a previous calendar year), entitlement to an option can be considered. For more information, refer to Options (Policy) and Options (Policy) Examples—Calculating Options with Lump Sum Payments CPP/QPP enhancement As of January 1, 2019, the Department began phasing in the CPP enhancement; a new component of the CPP. The enhancement is not a separate benefit, but a "top-up" to the original, now referred to as the base component of the CPP. The CPP enhancement is called "Additional CPP". As of January 1, 2019, the QPP was also enhanced in a way that mirrors the CPP enhancement. Provisions were made in both provincial and federal legislation to ensure coordination of the enhanced portions of the CPP and the QPP. Gradual increases to CPP or QPP contribution rates will take place over a 7-year period (2019 to 2025). Starting in June 2022, clients who made valid contributions in January 2019 or later will start to receive the first additional component of their benefit, including any retroactive amounts. Those who begin receiving a benefit in June 2022 or later will be paid the first additional component as part of their regular monthly amount. The lump sum payments received are to be treated as described in the CPP/QPP Lump Sum Payments section above. In CPMS , the Account Overview, the Payables and the Receivables screens will display the breakdown of the base and first additional benefit amounts; however, the payment will be sent to the client as one total amount. Be sure to use the total CPP monthly amount when estimating CPP benefits. For more information, Payment of the first Additional Portion of the CPP Enhancement Pension income splitting Updated To lower a couple's joint tax liability, the Income Tax Act allows a senior to share their pension income with a lower-income spouse or a common-law partner. The eligible pension income is restricted to funds from private pension sources. The pension income splitting provision can have a negative impact on certain couples who are having their benefits calculated based on an estimate of their current income but elected to split their pension income in the base calendar year. When a couple is disadvantaged by the pension income split, the income reported on Line 11600 of the spouse or common-law partner who is not reporting an event must be manually removed from the base calendar year if the option is approved. It is effective the same month as the effective date of the option. Before the income is removed, the spouse or common-law partner who has the income on Line 11600 must submit a new statement of income or a GIS or ALW (Pension Income Splitting - Option situation - Consent to remove a transferred amount ) (ISP-3034) form to consent to the removal of the pension income split amount. If the option is cancelled (e.g. the client did not retire or it is determined that an optionable event has not happened), you must manually return Block 2 ( CRA income from Line 11600) of the spouse or common-law partner’s base calendar year income back to the original income amount that was declared. Cúram will perform a recalculation of the entitlement using the base calendar year income. This may result in an overpayment for the client and their spouse or common-law partner. Pension income unduly received Updated If a client has reported that they are repaying or have repaid pension income that was unduly received, an option may be granted for the reduction or termination of the pension if : the repayment is in a subsequent year to the event. the client is negatively impacted by the receipt of the benefits when calculating an option for another event. If the client received and repaid benefits in the same year and there is no other event, an option is not granted because the benefit and repayment offset each other and the client has not suffered a loss of pension income. The granting of an option also depends on how the repayment will appear on the client’s T4, because this can affect how an estimate is calculated. If the repayment is made while the client is still in receipt of the benefit, the net amount of benefits will appear on the T4 on the benefit line. If the repayment was made after the benefit ended, the repayment amount will appear in a separate box on the T4 and may be on a separate line for CRA income. If the repayment of benefits in the CRA income appears in Block 9, it is treated like all other income appearing on Block 9 and is not to be included in the estimated income. For example, for CPP pension income, generally the repayment of benefits happens by monthly recovery while the pension is still in pay. Therefore, the net amount of the benefit will appear on Line 11400 of the CRA income (Block 1). However, for Employment Insurance (EI) benefits, if the repayment occurs while the client is still in receipt of benefits, the net amount will appear on line 11900 of the CRA income (Block 3) and can be included in the estimate. If the repayment happens after the benefits have ended, the repayment will appear as a deduction on Line 23200 of the CRA income (Block 9) and is not included in the estimate, but will appear in the applicable base calendar year income. For more information, refer to Options (Policy) . For examples of the various ways this repayment can affect an option, Options (Policy) Examples—Options with Pension Income Unduly Received La Commission des normes de l'équité de la santé et de la sécurité du travail La Commission des normes de l'équité de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) is the provincial workers’ compensation benefits program in Quebec. CNESST is paid biweekly and calculated using a daily rate. The annual amount received is reported in Block 10 on the T5007 slip. If the accident that has resulted in the receipt of benefits occurs before the beneficiary is 64 years of age, they will continue to receive regular benefits until they reach 65. Beginning on the beneficiary’s 65th birthday, the benefit will begin to decrease by 25% for the next 4 years, ending at age 68. Each 25% reduction is an optionable event. CNESST is adjusted each year on the anniversary date of the day the worker became unable to work as a result of the accident. This adjustment is called the annual revalorization. The calculation of this adjustment takes into account the consumer price index, as well as the amount of gross annual income that was used as a basis for calculating the benefit, which is specific to each client. These 2 factors are used every year to set a client's adjustment rate. Generally, this increases the benefits. However, for some years, the small increase in the consumer price index contributes to the reduction of benefits for some CNESST recipients. This reduction is not optionable. If the accident that has resulted in the receipt of benefits occurs after the beneficiary is 64 years of age, they will receive benefits for 4 years after the date of the accident. The decrease of benefits at 25% per year will begin after the first year, on the anniversary date of the day the worker became unable to work as a result of the accident. The annual adjustment of benefits and the decrease will occur at the same time. Employment Insurance benefits Updated EI benefits are calculated on a weekly basis and paid bi-weekly, in arrears. An individual will therefore receive their benefit payments after the entitlement period it covers. For example, a benefit payment received on July 15, 2022 is for the entitlement period of June 26 to July 9, 2022. When calculating an option for an event (e.g. retirement from employment) and EI benefits are included in the estimate calculation, you must include the amount of benefits received after the event and not the entitlement periods. When reviewing Full Text Screens (FTS) for EI information, use the amount that appears in the Gross column not the Net column, even if the client did not receive the gross amount for that payment. Using the net amount could put the client in an overpayment situation when the reconciliation is performed. When the reconciliation is performed, the net amount (plus taxes) will be used. If the client did not receive the gross amount for each payment, they will receive an underpayment at this time. Alternatively, when processing an option and EI benefit payments ending is the event, the EI benefits are considered terminated when the entitlement period ends, not when the last payment is received. The event date and the effective date for the termination of EI benefits are the first month of no entitlement. If entitlement to EI benefit payments ends in December, but the final payment is received in January of the following year, the final payment is not included in the estimate calculation. As this income will also appear in the base calendar year for the payment period immediately following the option periods, you must create and defer a Manual – Evidence Verification Request task to manually remove it immediately before the affected payment period. For more information on estimating EI income, Options (Policy) FTS FTS is the system used by the EI program for all EI claim-related information. Access to FTS is available to designated staff in the regions to obtain EI information for option processing. To determine the entitlement weeks and payment dates for an individual, review the Payments tab in FTS. The entitlement weeks are in the Report Week column. The dates found in the Date Processed column identify payments that will be reflected on the Statement of Employment Insurance and Other Benefits (T4E) slip. This date is considered the date the payment was received. All payments processed in a particular year will be displayed on that year’s T4E. For example, if a payment for a reporting week in 2021 was not processed until 2022, the payment is considered income in 2022 rather than 2021 and will appear on the 2022 T4E slip. COVID-19 emergency benefits In response to the COVID-19 pandemic, the Government of Canada introduced emergency benefits to support Canadians by providing temporary income support for workers (employed and self-employed) who were directly impacted by the pandemic. These emergency benefits are: Employment Insurance Emergency Response Benefit (EI ERB); Canada Emergency Response Benefit (CERB); Canada Recovery Benefit (CRB); Canada Recovery Caregiving Benefit (CRCB); Canada Recovery Sickness Benefit (CRSB); and Canada Worker Lockdown Benefit (CWLB). For income-tested benefits, this income is treated differently depending on the year it is received. If you are processing an option that is affected by emergency benefits, refer to COVID-19: Interim Measures—Emergency Benefits (Action) for information on how to treat the income. COVID-19: Interim Measures—Emergency Benefits (Action) Registered Retirement Income Fund payments An individual must convert all the money in their Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP) into retirement income by December 31 of the year they turn 71 years old. The individual can choose one or a combination of the following retirement income choices: cash the RRSP; purchase a retirement annuity; convert the RRSP to a Registered Retirement Income Fund (RRIF). Many individuals choose to convert the RRSP to a RRIF. An individual may have as many RRIFs as they want and they may transfer money from one RRIF to another at any time. An individual must withdraw a minimum amount from the RRIF(s) each year, according to the formulae included in the Income Tax Act. There is no maximum withdrawal limit. An individual can determine their own withdrawal rate and schedule (i.e. annual, semi-annual, quarterly, monthly or weekly withdrawal periods). An individual may also change the rate and schedule of their withdrawals at any time during the course of a year. Most individuals make monthly withdrawals. A RRIF payment year is always a calendar year that is divided into periods. The period is based on the frequency of payments. For more information regarding RRIF payments and options, refer to Options (Policy) and Options (Policy) Examples—Calculating Options with RRIF Payments Lump Sum Pension Income Updated Lump sum payments that fall under the definition of pension income may qualify for an option. However, these lump sum payments are treated differently than regular pension income payments. Lump sum payments are often declared on Line 13000 (other income) of a pensioner’s Income Tax and Benefit Return. These payments can include a retroactive lump sum payment, an amount replacing future payments or a one-time payment. When you are determining whether to include or exclude the lump sum payment income in the estimate calculation, you must consider: when the lump sum payment was received; and whether other optionable events happened during the same calendar year or are being calculated in the same payment period. For more information, refer to Options (Policy) and Options (Policy) Examples—Calculating Options with Lump Sum Payments

Cúram will perform the option calculation based on the estimated income details that have been data captured. Cúram will use the estimated income evidences to calculate blocks 1, 2, 3, 7, 8 and 9. You must capture all income from these blocks as estimated income evidence, including non-optionable income from Block 9 received in the base income year. This income is automatically combined with the base year income for blocks 4, 5 and 6 to determine the total estimated income. This total estimated income is compared to the total base year income and the most advantageous income is used to calculate entitlement for the income tested benefit during the option period. You must review and analyze the provided information to ensure it is as complete and accurate as possible. You must ensure that the details of all the applicable events have been recorded to avoid overpayments when the estimated income is compared and reconciled with the actual income in the following year. Generally, when an option is processed for an event, two statements of estimated income are required. A current year option calculation is performed for the statement of estimated income that coincides with the calendar year that the event occurs in. Then a previous year option calculation is performed for the statement of estimated income that follows the calendar year that the event occurs in. The exception to this is when an option is effective January. As mentioned previously, only one statement of estimated income is required when an option is effective January, but depending on the type of event, the calculations to perform are different. If the individual retired from employment or self-employment in the month of December, the event is considered to have occurred in December but the option is effective January. Since the event occurred in the calendar year immediately before the year of the statement of estimated income, a previous year option calculation is performed for January to June and again for the period from July to the following June, resulting in only 2 previous year option calculations. If the individual’s pension income reduced or terminated in January, the event is considered to have occurred in January and the option is effective January. Since the event occurred in the same calendar year as the year of the statement of estimated income, a current year option calculation is performed for the period from January to June and again for the period from July to the following June, resulting in only 2 current year option calculations. Post-mortem option calculations When performing the option calculations for the year that the individual passed away, the estimated income is prorated or calculated for the entire year, as though the individual is still alive. This ensures that the estate receives the correct entitlement of benefits that would have been paid if the death did not occur. This formula uses the income that was received after the optionable event and prorates it over a full year. The following calculation is used: Cúram will compare the result of this calculation to the result of the proration calculation and the lesser of the two calculations is used in the estimate calculation. This ensures that the estimate will never be higher than what the client could actually receive in a year. For examples of prorating using the formula, Examples—Current Year Option Prorating Calculations Employment and self-employment income If the event is not retirement, the full amount of employment or self-employment income the client expects to receive in the calendar year, minus the calculated earnings exemption, is included in the calculation. If the event is a reduction of employment income (e.g. reduced hours, new position at a reduced rate of pay), only the employment and self-employment income that the client expects to receive after the month of retirement, minus the calculated earnings exemption, will be included in the calculation. If the event is retirement, any employment income related to the retirement that is received in the same calendar year must be excluded from the calculation, such as: severance pay; vacation pay; sick leave benefits; retroactive salary adjustments; bonuses and commissions; and disposition of business assets. If the individual has retired from employment but is on leave immediately following their retirement date (e.g. sick leave, vacation leave), they are still receiving a regular income until the leave has ended. The event date for the retirement in this situation is the last day for which the individual receives regular salary or wages. If the individual receives income from more than one employment source and has retired from only one, the full amount of employment or self-employment income the individual expects to receive from the other employment sources in the calendar year, minus the calculated earnings exemption, is included in the calculation. If this breakdown is not provided on the ISP-3041 form, you can obtain the information over the phone. Other income Include all other income from the base calendar year in the estimate calculation. If there is income in the base calendar year and you are unsure of the source (e.g. Line 13000), review the file or contact the individual to clarify and confirm what the source is. If the income is a pension income that is affected by the option, remove it from the base calendar year income and include it in the estimate calculation as applicable. For example, if the individual has retired from employment or self-employment, retiring allowances (severance pay), disposition of business assets and profit sharing would appear in Line 13000. Although this employment income is found in Block 9, it cannot be used as part of the estimated income when calculating an option based on retirement and must be removed from the base calendar year income. Once you have confirmed the source of income in Block 9, you must manually enter it into Cúram when you enter the pension and employment incomes. You must identify whether the income is non-optionable annual income from the base calendar year or optionable income that must be included in the estimated income calculation (e.g. alimony or support payments). Previous year option calculation Pension income The estimated pension income for a previous year option is not prorated. All pension income that is received for the calendar year is estimated as it is expected to be received. The following formula is used for the calculation: Employment and self-employment income If the event is not retirement, you must include all employment and self-employment income received for the calendar year as it is expected to be received. If the event is retirement and the individual has reported subsequent employment income related to the retirement on the previous year option form, do not include it in the previous year option calculation. When the subsequent employment income related to the retirement, is included in the individual’s income for the payment period immediately following the previous year option, remove this income from the base calendar year by updating the manually entered income and excluding this amount. If the subsequent income is received more than a year after the last option ending, it cannot be removed from the base calendar year income and must be included as income in the calculation of income-tested benefits. For self-employment, there are situations where an option can be granted for equipment sales related to the business in the following year or years after retirement. For more information, Options (Policy) Other income All other income from the base calendar year is included in the estimate calculation. If there is income in the base calendar year and you are unsure of the source (e.g. Line 13000), review the file or contact the individual to clarify and confirm that it is not a pensionable income that should be removed from the base calendar year and, if applicable, estimated. For example, if the individual retired from employment or self-employment, retiring allowances (severance pay), disposition of business assets and profit sharing would appear in Line 13000. Although this employment income is found in Block 9, it cannot be used as part of the estimated income when calculating an option based on retirement. Once you have confirmed the source of income in Block 9, you must manually enter it into Cúram when you enter the pension and employment incomes. You must identify whether the income is non-optionable annual income from the base calendar year or optionable income that must be included in the estimated income calculation (e.g. alimony or support payments).

Cúram will perform the option calculation based on the estimate details that have been data captured. Therefore, when you receive a Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form, you must review and analyze the information provided to ensure it is complete, accurate and that the details of all the applicable events have been recorded. This step is also important to avoid overpayments when the estimated income is reconciled with the actual income in the following year. You must ensure that the applicant has reported income amounts from all the sources that they expect to receive income from for the estimated year by comparing the income that is reported on the ISP-3041 form to the income that was received in the previous year. Once you confirm that all income sources have been estimated on the ISP-3041 form, confirm that the benefit rates and payment amounts reported on the statement (if converted to an annual amount) are consistent with the annual amount reported in the previous year. Allow for fluctuations due to cost of living increases or exchange rates. If the related previous or current year option has already been processed, compare the information that is provided on the current statement with the information that was previously provided and investigate any discrepancies, such as: event type; event date; benefit amounts; and sources of income. Examples—Options With Missing Information and Discrepancies In the payment period following the estimate year, the client must provide the actual income for the estimate year. When the actual income is available at the time the estimate is being processed, you must compare the actual income information with the estimate details and manually reconcile the incomes before data capturing the information in Cúram. For more information on how to manually reconcile the income and to indicate in Cúram if this has been done, go to the Reconciliation of an option section below. If you are processing the option after renewal in the year following the estimate year and the actual income has not been received yet, you must request it before finalizing the option. If the income has still not been received by October after renewal, advise the individual that the option cannot be processed until the actual income is received. Process the option as usual after the required client income information is received. If the required income is not received by October, add a Is not entitled override to the income-tested benefit in the system for the current payment period to prevent Cúram from automatically calculating entitlement when the income is received. Once the required income is received in Cúram, a task will be generated to review the account, process the option, remove the override and determine entitlement for the affected payment period. For more information about the reconciliation process that occurs in the year after the option was processed, go to the Reconciliation of an Option section below.

The effective date of an option is based on: the type of event; when the event occurred ; and the frequency of payments (for pension income). A Current Year Option is effective: the month following the month of retirement; the first month the pension is not paid (for Employment Insurance benefits, the option is effective the first month of no entitlement ); or the month the reduction of the pension income takes place. A Previous Year Option is effective: July of the payment period that follows the calendar year of the event; or January when the individual retires in December. For more information on effective dates, refer to Options (Policy) and Options (Policy) Examples—Option Effective Date

The effective date of an option is the month following the month of retirement, the first month in which the pension is not paid, or the month the reduction of the pension income takes place. Effective date of retirement The date of retirement is the last day the individual receives income from that office or employment. This could occur in the month the employee actually performs the duties of the position, or it could be the last day the employee receives regular salary or wages, i.e. where an employee is on leave and is being paid regular salary or wages (e.g. vacation or sick leave) until the date of actual retirement. For a self-employed person, the date of retirement is the last day in which they actively carry on that business or terminate their business activities. Where an individual gives the first day of a month as the date of retirement, it should be clarified as to when the actual last day of employment or self-employment occurred. Effective date of option The option is effective in the month following retirement. Effective date of termination or reduction of pension income For pension income, the loss is suffered: in the first month or periodic payment period the individual receives no pension; or the first month or periodic payment period they receive a reduced pension. Effective date of option The option is effective for the first month or periodic payment period in which the pension is either not paid or is paid at a reduced rate. If the periodic payment is annual , the effective date of the option is the first month of the year ( January ) in which the payment is reduced or the first month of the year ( January ) the pension is not paid. If the periodic payment is semi-annual , the effective date of the option is the first month of the 6-month period ( January and July ) in which the payment is reduced or the first 6-month period ( January and July ) the pension is not paid. If the periodic payment is quarterl y, the effective date of the option is the first month of the 3-month period ( January, April, July, and Octobe r) in which the payment is reduced or the first 3-month period ( January, April, July and October ) the pension is not paid. If the payment is monthly , the effective date of the option is the month the payment is reduced or the first month the pension is not paid.

A client who was granted an option must provide their actual income information for the following payment period by: completing an Income Tax and Benefit Return so the income can be provided by the CRA ; or submitting a Statement of Income for the Renewal of the Guaranteed Income Supplement, the Allowance or Allowance for the Survivor for payment period of July (20XX) to June (20XX) with Information Sheet (ISP-3026) form. Reconciliation is required to validate the actual income against the estimated income that was previously calculated. You must review and question any discrepancies that you are unable to resolve by reviewing the information on file, to assure the accuracy of the benefit rate paid. The only option situation that does not require a reconciliation is the option granted to a client who has since passed away and the required actual income has not been received by the Department. As statements of income may be waived, the income information received from the CRA is treated as a statement of income. When actual income is available at the time that the estimate is being processed, you must manually reconcile the estimated and actual incomes before activating the evidence in Cúram. It is expected that the actual income required to perform the reconciliation should be received by July following the year of the estimate for the renewal of the income-tested benefit. If the required income is not available at the time of processing and it should be, defer the Estimated Income 3041 task until October. If by October the actual income is not received and the appropriate requests for the income have been sent, the client will no longer be entitled to the option until they submit the required information. The entitlement for the option period must be recalculated using the base calendar year income. Add an Is not entitled override to the system for the current payment period. Once the income is received, a task will be generated to review the account. When the required income information is received, the override must be removed and the option can be processed again along with the reconciliation for the affected period. Refer to Option Reconciliation—Follow-up Income not Received (Action) for the procedures to follow-up on these accounts. A client who was granted an option must submit their income for the following payment period so that an option reconciliation can be performed. Reporting of actual income must include all income that is considered income for GIS, ALW or ALWS benefit purposes regardless of how that income was used in the option calculation. You must compare the statement of actual income for the base calendar year against the statement of estimated income previously made. You must question any discrepancies that you are unable to resolve when reviewing the information on file to ensure the accuracy of the benefit rate paid. Options are generally processed in 2 parts: current year and previous year. Each part of the option must be reviewed and reconciled individually, based on the respective year of the estimated income. For more information regarding option reconciliations, Reconcile Options For options in the OAS Online system with a C or P option code, National Headquarters will perform regular scans from April to July of each year to determine if a CRA income feed has been received. A final scan will be performed in October. If the Department has not received the required income, a PWS work item will be created in the appropriate mail processing centre for follow-up. To identify these items, a unique barcode will be added to PWS: NHQOPTRECALC-CYY-NOINCOME for current year options; and NHQOPTRECALC-PYY-NOINCOME for previous year options. Once it has been confirmed that the Department has not received the income required to perform the option reconciliation, the period previously paid on the estimated income may have to be reverted to the original base calendar year income, and the entitlement recalculated accordingly.

When there is an optionable event, a completed and signed Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form must be received by the Department before an option can be granted, even if the actual income for this year has already been received. Generally, an ISP-3041 form must be completed for each estimated calendar year. No other forms are acceptable. The ISP-3041 form has all the information that is required to calculate the estimated income. It also tells the individual that they are responsible for estimating their income as accurately as possible, and that the consequence of underestimating their income may be an overpayment that they must repay. Refer to Options (Policy) for more information regarding the requirement for an ISP-3041 form. Options (Policy)

The client may declare an optionable event. However, if you have reason to believe that an optionable event has occurred and the client did not declare it, a Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form must be sent. You may discover optional events during a review of: a GIS application or statement of income; an ISP-3041 form submitted for a different event; CPP and if available, QPP pension or benefit entitlement in ITRDS ; income received from the CRA ; a task created in Cúram due to an income variance; annual pension amounts provided by the foreign institution; or information that a client provided by letter, by telephone, or during a visit to a Service Canada Centre. In the case of a couple, the ISP-3041 form is sent to the individual who experienced the loss or reduction, even if they do not receive OAS benefits. When determining if you need to send an ISP-3041 form, you must verify whether the event has already happened or if the event will happen in the future. If the event has already happened and the time limits for submitting a statement of estimated income have not elapsed, you must immediately send the required forms to the individual who experienced the loss. Time Limit Tables for Submission of a Statement of Estimated Income If the event has not happened yet, there are situations where a form can be sent to the individual before the event or can be accepted as reported on a completed ISP-3041 form. Future Optionable Events—Sending and Accepting the ISP3041 Form Before the Event When an event is going to happen in the future and the client does not know the details at the time of reporting, it is preferred that the necessary forms are sent when the event has actually occurred. When multiple events happen in the same calendar year, a single ISP-3041 form can be used if the dates of all the events within that year can be accurately recorded on the form. If the client has another event that has not been recorded, then you must obtain another ISP-3041 form for the same calendar year. If the event is related to CPP income, all information for a CPP-related event is available in ITRDS and CPMS . Therefore, if a CPP-related event is identified and not included on the form, you can include: the event in the Statement of Estimated Income evidence in Cúram; and the details of the event in ITRDS notes. It is important that the Department has an ISP-3041 form that accurately reflects the client’s estimated income for the applicable calendar year. An ISP-3041 form is automatically sent by Cúram when an event occurred in the current month or a future month and a Retirement or Pension Reduction evidence record is created. If the event is for a future month the form will be sent at the beginning of the month in which the event occurs. If the event date has already passed and is within the prescribed timelines, you must send the applicable form manually. For income-tested benefit purposes, the option provision offers the individual and/or their spouse or common-law partner a choice to have their income calculated based on an estimate or based on their income from the base calendar year. The individual must provide a written request to calculate their income using an estimate. To process an option, an individual must submit their income for the base calendar year, and must provide it via a statement of income, or via the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) income feed. An individual must also submit the Statement of Estimated Income after Retirement or Reduction in Pension Income for the Year 20XX (ISP-3041) form for the year of the event. This form meets the legislative requirements and provides the authorization to calculate the individual's income based on their estimated income. The statement of estimated income form must capture all the information required, including: a clear request for an option; a statement confirming the month of retirement or loss or reduction of pension income; a statement of estimated employment or self-employment; or pension income for the year of the event or for the year following the event. The form also informs the individual of his or her responsibilities to estimate their income as accurately as possible, and that the consequence of underestimating their income could be an overpayment that must be repaid. If multiple events occur in the same calendar year, a single form can be used if the dates of all of the events within that year are recorded on the form. If the individual has another event that has not been recorded, then another statement for the same calendar year would have to be obtained. It is important that the Department has a statement of estimated income form that accurately reflects the individual's estimated income for the calendar year. If an event occurs in the future and the individual does not know the details at the time of reporting, the necessary form(s) is sent at the time the event actually occurred. Any entitlement is then recalculated after the form is received from the individual.
An option can be applied retroactively if it is determined that the individual is eligible for income-tested benefits for the option period. For more information, Options (Policy)

A retroactive option may be granted once the following conditions are met: There is eligibility for income-tested benefits for the period of the option. An application or statement of income must have already been submitted for the income-tested benefit or the data transfer of income must have already been received from the Canada Revenue Agency. Receipt of the option form is within the legislated timeframes.
