When one spouse or common-law partner receives or would receive an OAS pension and a Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS) benefit under Rate Table 3, and the other spouse or common-law partner’s OAS pension (and possibly a GIS benefit) is approved, the first spouse or common-law partner continues to be entitled to receive the GIS benefit amount as calculated under Rate Table 3 minus the second spouse or common-law partner’s OAS pension (and a GIS benefit, if applicable) amount as determined under Rate Table 2. Before considering or adjusting a payment based on Rate Table 1, the following situations must be determined: Any couple such as individuals living apart for reasons beyond their control; A separation; or The death of one spouse or common-law partner during the payment year. Once the most beneficial rate is determined, the resulting amount must be compared with the benefit on Rate Table 1. The most beneficial rate can then be determined by verifying if the rate on Rate Table 1 is greater than the rate calculated by determining the adjustment.

This policy ensures a married or common-law couple will at least maintain a total amount of benefits at a rate equivalent to what they would receive or were receiving as a spouse or common-law partner of a non-pensioner. When it is to their advantage, the spouses of a married or common-law couple who are both pensioners may be paid using separate rate tables. This can occur when the non-pensioner spouse or common-law partner becomes eligible for an OAS pension and a Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS) benefit. For example, one spouse or common-law partner receives an OAS pension and a GIS benefit at Rate Table 2, while the other spouse or common-law partner receives an OAS pension and a GIS benefit at Rate Table 3, less the OAS and GIS amounts received by the other spouse or common-law partner. The right for both pensioners to receive a pension is protected, and this protection ensures that each pensioner’s right to receive a pension is not detrimental to the other spouse or common-law partner’s current benefit. The total OAS pension and GIS entitlement paid to one pensioner at the rate of a married or common-law pensioner with a non-pensioner spouse is also protected.

Entitlement to income-tested benefits under the OAS Act such as the GIS, the ALW and the ALWS is based on: the beneficiary's current marital status; and net income received in the base calendar year. When the beneficiary has a spouse or common-law partner, their combined income is used for calculating their GIS and/or ALW . Exceptions occur when: the couple is separated for reasons beyond their control; or one of them is incarcerated. Income under the OAS Act is calculated in accordance with the Income Tax Act . The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) assesses income on an annual basis from the filing of income tax and benefit returns. The income used to assess income-tested benefits is from the previous calendar year and the benefit is paid on that amount for the next payment period, which runs from July 1 of the current year to June 30 of the following year. Income-tested benefits are adjusted on an annual basis. However, certain sources of income, as outlined under the Income not considered section below, are excluded from the calculation under the OAS Act. Although some sources of income are not taxable, they are still defined as income under the Income Tax Act and, therefore, must be considered as income under the OAS Act. Deductions allowed by CRA for tax purposes are also allowed under the OAS Act to reduce a beneficiary's income. Some additional deductions specific to the OAS Act may further enable a beneficiary to become entitled to receive a GIS, ALW or ALWS or a higher benefit payment amount. When an individual's income decreases due to retirement or a reduction or loss of pension income, the GIS, ALW or ALWS entitlement may be calculated based on an estimate of certain sources of income for the current calendar year rather than on the base calendar year income. This is referred to as an 'option'. This estimated income is added to any other type of income from the base calendar year.

Each year, an individual's ongoing entitlement to the GIS, ALW and ALWS benefits must be reviewed based on their latest income. Individuals will be notified by letter about their ongoing entitlement in a staggered approach, based on letter type and printer capabilities. This year, letters will be mailed in July and August. In most cases, individuals remain entitled to their income-tested benefit. However, their payments could increase or decrease depending on their income compared to the previous year. For example, an individual could see a decrease in benefits if their 2023 income is higher than their 2022 income. In other cases, an individual's benefit will not continue for one of the following three reasons: Their income or combined income exceeded the maximum amount (excess income); They indicated that they do not wish to receive the benefit; or Service Canada did not receive all of the necessary income information. Suspension letters requesting income information will include a Statement of income for the Renewal of the GIS, the ALW or ALWS for payment period of July (2024) to June (2025) with Information Sheet (ISP-3026 form) to give clients the means to provide their income information and renew their benefits. The letters informing clients of their entitlement to benefits for the 2024 to 2025 payment period will be mailed in 3 phases: The first phase will be the suspension letters. These letters will be sent starting the week of July 15, 2024; The second phase will be the entitlement letters. These letters will be mailed to individuals once the mailing of the suspension letters is complete. The anticipated start date is July 23, 2024; and The third phase will be the non-entitlement letters . The anticipated start date is August 13, 2024. These letters will be sent to individuals who are GIS for Life but who were not receiving a benefit in the 2023 to 2024 payment period and are not entitled to a benefit in the 2024 to 2025 payment period. The following entitlement letters will be mailed to the beneficiary: GIS/ ALW / ALWS Entitlement Letter (ISP-3057) GIS Suspension Letter (ISP-3067) GIS Suspension Letter - IO (ISP-3067-IO) ALW / ALWS Suspension Letter (ISP-3068) ALW / ALWS Suspension Letter - IO (ISP-3068-IO) GIS/ ALW / ALWS Non-Entitlement Letter (ISP-3056)

The income-tested benefits under OAS, including the GIS, ALW , ALWS , renew every July based on the previous year income. You can obtain the income through the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) income feed or through a Statement of income for the Renewal of the Guaranteed Income Supplement, the Allowance or Allowance for the Survivor for payment period of July (20XX) to June (20XX) with Information Sheet (ISP-3026) form submitted by the client. Currently, if the department does not receive a client's or their spouse/common-law partner's income on time, they cannot be auto renewed for GIS. The GIS Potential report on OAS Basic Accounts with GIS for Life lists active and pending OAS accounts where income from the CRA was received from the one-way feed and is low enough for potential entitlement to the GIS, ALW and ALWS . This potential entitlement is based on income, or combined income (in the case of a couple), and the marital status. A delay in receiving income can occur if a client or their spouse or common-law partner does not file their taxes on time with CRA. GIS Potential work items are generated in PWS for accounts appearing on the report.

Individuals with the following will not be selected for automatic enrolment: a foreign residential address or a foreign tax withhold; a warning flag on file at the SIR (warning flags identify issues such as possible fraud, lost or stolen cards, or dormant files); a power of attorney on the individual's CPP file (each power of attorney agreement provides different rights and limitations). Additionally, selected individuals will not be automatically enrolled if, before their 65th birthday: they notify Service Canada that they have ceased or will cease to reside in Canada; they report inaccuracies in the information on the OAS Automatic Enrolment Notification letter (ISP-3009) or the OAS Automatic Enrolment Notification letter (ISP-3030) and no longer meet the eligibility requirements; or they decline the pension. In all of the above situations, the individual will be notified that an application is required.

Depending on the situation, pensioners approved for a partial pension can receive additional 40ths for accumulated periods of residence or an actuarially adjusted pension based on the number of 40ths at the earliest date of eligibility. Unless they decide otherwise, you must calculate each additional 40ths and actuarially adjusted pension to provide the individual with the most beneficial rate. As of July 2013, applicants who qualify for a partial pension and who have voluntarily deferred their pension or have applied late, must be advised of the amount of their pension with an actuarial adjustment and accumulated residence for the same period of time. If deferral is chosen by the individual, o r is the most advantageous payment option, the partial OAS pension is increased by a factor of 0.6% for each month an individual defers receipt of their OAS pension after the month of initial eligibility up to and including the month of approval of their OAS pension.

As of July 1, 2013, individuals may choose to voluntarily defer receipt of their OAS pension starting the month they are entitled to receive the pension. Individuals will only get credit for deferral from this month onward. Individuals who are eligible to receive a full pension may choose to defer their pension start date to receive the increased actuarial adjustment. Those who are eligible for a partial pension may also choose to defer their pension, and in some cases are given the choice of increasing their benefit amount based on: the actuarial adjustment; or additional 40ths for the accumulated periods of residence in Canada. Individuals are able to defer the start of their pension for a maximum of 60 months up to the month they turn 70 years of age . Individuals who choose to defer receipt of their pension will not be eligible to receive the Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS). I n addition, their spouse or common-law partner will not be eligible for the Allowanceduring the deferral period. The actuarially adjusted pension is based on the pension rate at the effective date of the full pension.

Mary turned 18 in October 2024. Mary was in full-time attendance at school beginning in September 2024. However, Mary did not submit a Declaration of Attendance at School or University (ISP-1401) form for September to December 2024. Mary submitted an ISP-1401 form for the winter semester only (beginning January 2025). Mary was not paid from November to December 2024 in the IA Legacy system. Mary then submitted an ISP-1401 form for the period from September to December 2024. As the second ISP-1401 form covers a school period before CPP IA migration, do not enter this school period into ITRDS . Only enter periods after January 2025. You must: Enter the school period after January 2025 in ITRDS . You must use the Super Program Exception Process functionality to data capture the child's benefit starting in January. Issue a manual priority payment for the 2 months that were previously withheld (November and December 2024). Update the client's notes.

Under the Department of Employment and Social Development Act , if the Minister considers it advisable and there is an agreement or contract between the Minister and other persons or bodies (e.g. a person or a non-government group or organization), personal information can be disclosed for the administration of any federal law or activity or any provincial law as per the terms of the contract.

To share personal information about an individual, there must be legal authority. The Department of Employment and Social Development Act , the Canada Pension Plan legislation (CPP legislation) and the Old Age Security Act (OAS Act) authorize the Department of Employment and Social Development to share or exchange an individual's personal information in the administration and the enforcement of the program for which the information was obtained or for another program. The Department of Employment and Social Development Act , the CPP legislation and the OAS Act enable the Minister to enter into agreements with the following for the purpose of information gathering for the administration or enforcement of a program: federal institutions; governments of provinces or territories and public bodies created under their laws; governments of foreign states; international organizations of foreign states; and other persons or bodies. The conditions for the exchange of information are set out in an Information Sharing Agreement (ISA) or a Memorandum of Understanding. Information can only be released as set out in the legislation or as per the terms of the agreement or contract. For specific information that can be released, Information Sharing Agreements Regional and Federal Tools

When the enhancement was first established in July 2011, the maximum amount was set at $50.00 per month ($600.00 per year) for those ALWS beneficiaries, with an annual income of up to $2,000. The enhancement amount was subject to quarterly indexation. Effective July 1, 2016, the maximum amount of the enhancement increased by $78.92 per month for those ALWS beneficiaries with an annual income (excludin g OAS benefits) of up to $2,000. This amount continues to be subject to quarterly indexation. For individuals with an annual income over $2,000, the enhancement amount is reduced by $1.00 for every $48.00 of annual income.

When the enhancement was first established in July 2011, the maximum amount for single OAS pensioners was set at $50.00 per month ($600.00 per year) for those with an annual income (excluding OAS benefits) of up to $2,000. This amount was subject to quarterly indexation. Effective July 1, 2016, the maximum amount of the enhancement increased by $78.92 per month for those with an annual income (excluding OAS benefits) of up to $2,000. The enhancement amount is subject to quarterly indexation. For individuals with an annual income over $2,000, the enhancement amount is reduced by $1.00 for every $48.00 of annual income.

Cúram will calculate and apply the total earnings exemption of $7,000. This exemption is calculated as follows: Determine the total combined income: Deduct $5,000 from the total combined income: Calculate 50% of the amount that exceeds $5,000: Add the $5,000 exemption to the 50% exempted amount: Since the total earnings exemption amount is equal to the total employment income amount, Cúram will apply the full exemption to the employment income block in the system. As of April 6, 2021, CPP processing staff will no longer record and apply cash receipts in CPMS. The National Accounts Receivable (NAR) team in the Chief Financial Officer Branch (CFOB) will record incoming payments into the Public Sector Collections and Disbursements (PSCD) system. Due to the automatic interface between PSCD and CPMS, this action will automatically update the client’s account in CPMS. Incoming payments refers to the process of receiving payments to pay off program debts. These payments can be received via automated or manual transactions by: walk-in; mail; online banking; in-person banking; recoupment; and withhold. These payments create an incoming payment file, which are uploaded to PSCD. Incoming payments recorded by the NAR team during the December calendar month will automatically update the debtor’s account in CPMS during the same calendar year. When PSCD interfaces with CPMS, it will update the debtor’s: payment history, year-to-date totals; benefit amounts; and receivables. As CPP no longer receives Notifications of Cash Receipts, if you need to verify if a payment was received from a client and applied by the NAR team in PSCD, View Incoming Payments Payment Clarification worklist Incoming payments that cannot be actioned by the NAR team due to missing or incomplete information will appear on the Payment Clarification worklist produced by PSCD. This worklist identifies work items that need further investigation by the CFOB before any payments can be applied to an account. Incoming payments that cannot be applied against a debt in PSCD for the following reasons will create a credit that will be refunded to the client by the NAR team: the client is not aware that the debt is paid in full and continues to make payments; a payment is received after a debt has been remitted; a bankruptcy or judgment was applied on the account for a previous date and payments were applied after that date; or a set-off was applied after the client paid the account. You will no longer create a manual priority payment to issue refunds; this action will now be completed by the NAR team. Payments that require a refund will have a status of Awaiting Section 20 approval on the Payment Clarification worklist in PSCD. Once the refund is investigated and approved by the NAR team, the credit (i.e. refund) displays a document type of RF (i.e. refund) in PSCD).

Effective January 2021, benefits were suspended if the 2019 income information required to renew the GIS, ALW or ALWS benefit ha d not been received and processed. For entitlement to these benefits to be renewed for the 2020-2021 payment year, clients must provide their 2019 income information, as well as their spouse or common-law partner's, if applicable. If a client who was paid benefits under the GIS Renewal 2020 interim measures provides their 2019 income information over the phone to a call centre agent, the agent will either: add the 2019 income to OAS online and create an urgent PWS Enquiry work item for the appropriate processing centre to issue the retroactive payment effective January 2021, or record the information on a GIS Renewal Telecentre Contact Report (ISP3088) form and send it to the appropriate processing centre by creating a PWS Enquiry work item for urgent processing. The client is required to submit a statement of income to the Department within 60 days. Once the statement of income is received, follow-up actions will be required by processing staff to reconcile the account for the period of July to December 2020. Further direction will be provided soon for establishing and recovering overpayments on accounts where the 2019 income information has not been received. Due to challenges faced during the COVID-19 pandemic and a different tax filing deadline, seniors may have experienced difficulties providing their income information to Service Canada to renew their income tested benefits in July 2020. For those reasons, an interim measure was implemented for clients where the 2019 income information required to renew their Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS), Allowance (ALW) or Allowance for the Survivor (ALWS) benefit in July 2020 was not received. In these cases, a monthly payment equal to the June 2020 payment was issued for up to 6 months. The individual continued receiving this payment until the required income information was received and processed, or until December 2020.

The automated process is designed to assist the regional processing centres with processing Canada Revenue Agency ( CRA ) Reassessment reports. During the process, the income is adjusted and an overpayment or underpayment letter is sent to the client. These automated letters are saved in the Corporate Correspondence Tool letter vault and are accessible by specific authorized individuals. The accounts considered for this process are active MS1 , 2 , 3 , 8 and 9 with a 3017 work item in Auto status in PWS . The automated process will proceed as follows: Identify 3017 work items in PWS that are Unassigned with an Auto status; Assign the work item in PWS to the BOT , which means Robotic Process Automation. The BOT usernames contain "UiPath" and/or "Pensions" followed by a number ; Apply the exception criteria below to determine if the automated process can continue; If yes, the automated process will go to Step 4 . Step 4 If no, the automated process will flag the work item as an exception for manual processing. In OAS Online, go to the CRA INCOME screen to obtain the new total income or combined total income if there is a spouse or common-law partner. On the INCOME screen, update the existing inco me for the client, spouse or common-law partner using the new income. On the RE-CALCULATION Input screen, add the ne w or combined total income to the income fields of the applicable months. Determine if there is any change in the client's, spouse's or common-law partner’s entitlement: If the recalculated net amount is negative , the automated process will: On the DEDUCTION screen in OAS Online, add the overpayment. Send the appropriate overpayment letter to the client . Add notes in ITRDS by user “BRPA” with details of the actions taken. If the recalculated net amount is positive, the automated process will: Perform the following steps in OAS Online: On the DEDUCTION screen in OAS Online, check for any existing outstanding overpayments for codes 01, 03 or 05 and remove any existing recovery rate for these codes; On the CASH RECEIPTS screen, apply the underpayment to any existing overpayment, if applicable; or If the outstanding balance remaining is an overpayment, the client will be notified of the new outstanding amount. If the outstanding balance remaining is an underpayment, it will be released online and the client will be notified. On the UNDERPAYMENT screen, issue the full balance of the underpayment. Send the appropriate letter to the client to notify them of the actions taken; and Add notes in ITRDS by user “BRPA” with details of the actions taken; or If the recalculated net amount is NIL (results in no change to the beneficiary’s entitlement), the automated process will add notes to ITRDS by user “BRPA” to indicate the recalculation was completed. Complete the work item in PWS with the following note: "Work item processed by Automation // Article de travail traité par Automatisation."

The automated process is designed to assist the regional processing centers with processing accounts from the CRA yearly variance report. During this process, the income is adjusted, underpayments are issued and a letter is sent to the client. These automated letters are then saved in the Corporate Correspondence Tool vault and are accessible by processing staff. The accounts considered for this process automation are active MS1 , MS2 and MS3 accounts with a Variance Rreport work item in Auto status in PWS. The automated process will proceed as follows: Identify the Variance Report work items in PWS that are Unassigned with an Auto status. Assign the work item in PWS to the automated process. The usernames used by the automation process contain "UiPath" or "Pensions" followed by a number. Apply the exception criteria below to determine if the automated process can continue: If yes , the automated process will go to Step 4 . Step 4 If no , the automated process will flag the work item as an exception for manual processing. In OAS Online, go to the CRA Income (CRA) screen to obtain the income needed from the estimated year and from the base calendar year. In ITRDS, determine if the client is in receipt of CPP benefits: If yes , the automation will access CPMS to obtain the client's monthly CPP rate for the years in review. If no , the automated process will flag the work item as an exception for manual processing. Calculate the new estimated income total. On the Re-Calculation Input (CAL) screen, determine the payment period and validate that the account status, marital status and payment income on the Re-Calculation screen were consistent. Add the new estimated total income to the Payment income field. Determine if there are any changes in the client's or the spouse or common-law partner's entitlement. If the recalculated net amount is positive , the automated process will do the following: Perform the following steps in OAS Online: On the Deductions (DED) screen, the automated process will verify for any existing outstanding overpayments for codes 01, 03 or 05 and remove any existing recovery rate for these codes. On the Cash receipts (CSH) screen, the automated process will apply the underpayment to any existing overpayment, if applicable. If the outstanding balance remaining is an overpayment, the client will be notified of the new outstanding amount. If the outstanding balance remaining is an underpayment, it will be released online and the client will be notified. On the Underpayment (OVP) screen, the automated process will issue the full balance of the underpayment. Send the appropriate letter to the client to notify them of the actions taken. Add notes in ITRDS from user "BRPA" with details of the actions taken. If the recalculated net amount is NIL (i.e. results in no change to the beneficiary's entitlement), the automated process will add notes to ITRDS by user "BRPA" to indicate the recalculation was completed. Complete the work item in PWS with the following note: "Work item processed by Automation // Article de travail traité par Automatisation."

The Receiver General informed Service Canada that their Foreign Service Provider, Bank of America, will be terminating cheque services in New Zealand by December 31, 2020 . Consequently, all banks in New Zealand have decided to eliminate cheque services. This includes cheques issued in NZD, EUR, USD and CAD currency. The last month to process cheques will be December 2020. A 6-month period will follow (up to June 30, 2021) to clear cheques. Public Services and Procurement Canada has already: sent a letter with a foreign direct deposit form to all those receiving a cheque in New Zealand in NZD, EUR, USD and CAD currency at the end of August or the beginning of September; sent a copy of the letter and a foreign direct deposit form to the Embassy to inform them of the upcoming change; updated the Countries of the World document; added a message to its Foreign Direct Deposit page; and added a message to its RG Enquiry and direct deposit automated responses. In addition, a follow-up letter with a foreign direct deposit form will be sent with the October monthly cheque payment.

The GIS Potential work items are created with Auto status and Unassigned in PWS . The accounts considered for this process are active Marital Status 1, 2, 3, 8 and 9 accounts. The automated process will: Identify GIS Potential work items in PWS that are Unassigned with an Auto status. Assign the work item in PWS to the automated process with usernames containing “ UiPath ” and/or Pensions” followed by a number. Apply early exception criteria to the client (and spouse or common-law partner account if MS = 2) to determine if the automated process can continue: If yes, the automated process will go to Step 4; (MS 8 or 9 accounts will be released prior to moving to next step). If no, the automated process will flag the work item as an exception for manual processing and return the work item to the Region in Active status. Copy and paste the income from the CRA INCOME screen to the client's INCOME screen in OAS Online . On the RE-CALCULATION screen, calculate entitlement retroactively to July of the current payment period for the client, spouse or common-law partner. Release any calculated underpayment owing to the client, spouse or common-law partner. Add a note in ITRDS by user “ BRPA ” and generate a letter to the client, spouse or common-law partner, and Complete the work item in PWS with the following note: Work item processed by Automation”. The automation tool uses delegated authorities that are in line with those of a Service Canada Benefits Officer ( SCBO ).

For week 1, the automated process will: Identify GIS automatic enrolment work items in PWS with barcodes related to GIS automatic enrolment Scenario 1 and ensure that the work items are Unassigned with Auto status. Assign the work item to itself. Apply the early exception criteria to the client and their spouse or common-law partner to determine if the automated process can continue: If yes , the automated process will go to Step 4 . Step 4 If no , the automated process will: flag the work item as an exception for manual processing; and return the work item to the Region in Active status. In OAS Online, create a NPS account for the client’s spouse or common-law partner. In the NPS account in ITRDS , add a note from user “BRPA”. In PWS , add a Bring Forward (BF) date of 7 days to the work item using the reason “Awaiting CRA Income”. For week 2, the automated process will: Retrieve the GIS automatic enrolment work item in Auto status with a BF date from PWS . Apply the exception criteria for week 2 to the auto-enrolled client and their spouse or common-law partner to determine if the automated process can continue: If yes , the automated process will go to Step 3 . Step 3 If no , the automated process will: flag the work item as an exception for manual processing; and return the work item to the Region in Active status. Perform the following actions in OAS Online: Check that OAS Online has received the CRA income information for both the auto-enrolled client and their spouse or common-law partner: If yes , the automated process will go to Step b . Step b If no , the work item will be returned to Auto status with a BF date in PWS of an added week. Copy and paste the income from the CRA Income ( CRA ) screen to the auto-enrolled client’s Income (INC) screen. For the auto-enrolled client, set the GIS for Life Flag to Y on the Change Client Info (GEN) screen. On the auto-enrolled client’s OAS –Auto Enrolment screen in ITRDS , set the GIS automatic enrolment indicator to Yes. In the auto-enrolled client’s account in ITRDS , add a note from user “BRPA”. In PWS , complete the work item with the following note: “Work item processed by Automation.”

For week 1, the automated process will: In PWS , identify the GIS automatic enrolment work items in PWS with barcodes related to GIS automatic enrolment Scenario 9 and ensure that the work items are Unassigned with Auto status. Assign the work item to itself. Apply the early exception criteria to the auto-enrolled client and their spouse or common-law partner to determine if the automated process can continue: If yes , the automated process will go to Step 4 . Step 4 If no , the automated process will: flag the work item as an exception for manual processing; and return the work item to the Region in Active status. Perform the following actions in OAS Online: On the Monetary (MON) screen, send a GIS application to the spouse or common-law partner. Request the CRA income for the spouse or common-law partner. Link the auto-enrolled client and spouse or common-law partner accounts together. In ITRDS , add a note to the spouse or common-law partner’s account from user “BRPA”. In PWS , add a Bring Forward (BF) date of 7 days to the work item using the reason “Awaiting CRA Income”. For week 2, the automated process will: From PWS , retrieve the GIS automatic enrolment work item in Auto status with a BF date. Apply the exception criteria for week 2 to the auto-enrolled client and their spouse or common-law partner to determine if the automated process can continue: If yes , the automated process will go to Step 3 . Step 3 If no , the automated process will: flag the work item as an exception for manual processing; and return the work item to the Region in Active status. Perform the following actions in OAS Online: Check for the CRA income information and ensure that it has been received for both the auto-enrolled client and their spouse or common-law partner: If yes , the automated process will go to Step b . Step b If no , the work item will be returned to Auto status with a BF date in PWS of an added week Copy and paste the income from the CRA Income ( CRA ) screen to the auto-enrolled client’s Income (INC) screen. On the auto-enrolled client’s Change Client Info (GEN) screen, set the GIS for Life Flag to Y . On the spouse or common-law partner’s Change Client Info (GEN) screen, set the GIS for Life Flag to N . On the auto-enrolled client’s OAS –Auto Enrolment screen in ITRDS , set the GIS automatic enrolment indicator to Yes . In ITRDS , add a note to the auto-enrolled client’s account from user “BRPA”. Complete the work item in PWS with the following note: “Work item processed by Automation.”

The MSCA Opt Out work items are created with Auto status and Unassigned in PWS. The accounts considered for this process are active MS1 , 2 , and 3 accounts . The automated process will: Identify MSCA Opt Out work items in PWS that are Unassigned with an Auto status. Assign the work item in PWS to the automated process, which means Robotic Process Automation. The automated process usernames contain "UiPath" and/or "Pensions" followed by a number. Apply most of the exception criteria below to determine if the automated process can continue. If yes, the automated process will go to Step 4 . Step 4 If no, the automated process will flag the work item as an exception for manual processing. Determine the Opt Out path: Opt out of OAS only or Opt out of OAS and GIS. If the client’s marital status is 3 and the spouse is NPS, the automated process will: access the spouse’s T4A screen in OAS Online; cancel the spouse’s NPS account. If spouse is not NPS, the automated process will flag the work item as an exception for manual processing; access the client’s T4A screen; cancel the client’s account; go to Step 5 ; or Step 5 If the client’s marital status is 1, the automated process will: access the client’s T4A screen; cancel the client’s account; go to Step 5 ; or Step 5 If the client’s marital status is 2 and the account status is 1, the automated process will: access the spouse’s Change Client Information (GEN) screen in OAS Online to confirm the GIS for Life Flag is N . If yes, the automated process will continue. If no, the automated process will flag the work item as an exception for manual processing. access the client’s T4A screen; cancel the client’s account; go to Step 5 ; or Step 5 Opt out of GIS only. The automated process will access the client’s Monetary (MON) screen in OAS Online. If income is not present, the automated process will continue to Step 5 . Step 5 If income is present, the automated process will: Remove the current or renewal income. Update the client’s GIS for Life Flag: If the client is MS1 or 3, the flag will be removed. If the client is MS2, and the spouse’s GIS for Life Flag is: Y , the client’s flag will be changed to an N to add a Calc Flag 4 on the account. N , the client’s flag will be removed. Go to Step 5 . Step 5 Add a note in ITRDS from user "BRPA", and Complete the work item in PWS with the following note: Work item processed by Automation. The automation tool uses delegated authorities that are in line with those of a Service Canada Benefits Officer.

When a couple is separated for 12 months or more, the PNSH ceases with the current processing month. If either spouse makes a request for reconsideration of the Department's decision to cease the PNSH with the current month, the Department must apply the legislation as it reads and effect the cessation with the month the event took place. If neither individual requests a reconsideration, remove all payables and receivables from both accounts in CPMS. If there is a reconsideration request asking the Department to cease the PNSH retroactively to 12 months after the separation or end of a common-law relationship, you must action the monetary in accordance with the Overpayment Policy, if: an individual’s payable is applied to their receivable; any remaining payable is issued to the individual; and any remaining receivable is recovered. The CPP legislation does not support this process.

Currently , operational policy and procedures direct processing staff that Pension Sharing (PNSH) ceases with the current processing month for cases when a couple is separated for 12 months or more. Effective immediately, operational policy and procedures have been updated to clarify the cessation date of PNSH of a Retirement pension under the Canada Pension Plan when a couple is separated for 12 months or more. As a result, the guidelines for recovering receivables and releasing payables when ceasing PNSH retroactively must be followed.

International Operations (IO) agents can transmit and receive correspondence with certain Canadian and foreign institutions using Canada Post's Connect.
IO processing sites have implemented the use of Canada Post's Connect service to exchange Protected B personal information with participating Canadian and foreign institutions.

Connect is a digital delivery platform that facilitates sending and receiving Protected B correspondence with one or multiple recipients. It enables secure collaboration through one common platform. IO staff can communicate through Connect to exchange: liaison forms; Canadian or foreign application forms; and supporting documents. Similar to an email inbox, Connect allows IO staff to create "conversations" with specific recipients and manage messages with replies and notifications. Forms and documents can be uploaded to the Connect platform for secure electronic delivery to a recipient. The Connect procedures for exchanging information with Canadian and foreign institutions are largely the same as the current procedures. The only difference is the elimination of the outgoing physical copy of correspondence by mail unless the recipient requests it. For each participating institution, 2 conversations will be created to facilitate document transfer and reduce the quantity of documents in each conversation. They conversations are as follows: one for processing staff to upload outgoing correspondence; and one for support staff to retrieve incoming correspondence.

Connect is a digital delivery platform that facilitates the sending and receiving of Protected B correspondence with one or multiple recipients. It enables secure collaboration through one common platform. Currently, when IO staff communicate with Canadian and foreign institutions to exchange information and applications, it is done through mail. With Connect, this exchange will happen digitally and will significantly decrease timeframes associated with the receipt of information as well as help streamline service delivery operations.

When the Department receives an unsigned paper application, form or written request that does not meet the requirements to be a valid pension and/or benefits CPP or OAS application, and reasonable attempts to obtain a signature or an application are unsuccessful, these are treated as correspondence and not an application. In cases where the application is determined to be invalid, the file must be administratively closed, and the applicant must be informed in writing. Reconsideration rights are not included as a valid application has not been received.

A valid application for OAS purposes is a departmental OAS pension application form with the applicant's signature. A valid application for CPP benefits is a departmental application form or a written request that clearly identifies the applicant, the CPP benefits requested and the applicant's signature. OAS and CPP provisions are not considered applications. OAS options are considered a statement, while CPP provisions are considered a request.

You must administratively close the file if you do not receive a valid application after all attempts to obtain one have been made within the bring forward periods. The departmental form or written statement for a benefit is now considered correspondence and not an application. Since you are not making an eligibility decision, reconsideration rights do not apply and are not included in the letter to the applicant. The appropriate letter to stop the review and administratively close the file informs the applicant their file is closed and they will need to reapply if they wish to receive a benefit in the future.

An application under CPP and OAS must meet certain criteria to be valid before making an eligibility decision. When an invalid application or intent to apply is received, the Department communicates with the applicant to gather the missing components to make an application valid. If the application remains invalid, the Department administratively closes the file. For clarity, "application" used in this article includes all pensions and benefits applications for all program benefits as well as a written request for a CPP program benefit. As of May 28, 2021, individuals can apply for ALW and ALWS benefits online through My Service Canada Account portal if they: are aged 59 + 1 month to age 65 + 11 months; and do not have a third party representative (trustee or power of attorney) on file. If any of the above criteria are not met, the applicant is directed to an "Unable to continue" page indicating why they cannot apply online. The message offers a "contact us" link that points to the Department's website and provides contact information, as well as information on how to submit a paper application. If all of the above criteria are met, the applicant can complete and submit their application online. Domestic addresses and telephone number updates through the online application are captured directly into ITRDS . Applicants with a foreign address on file are advised that an incorrect address may result in payment or follow-up letters not being delivered correctly. They are advised to contact the Department to update their address information before using the online service. Soon, individuals will have 3 additional e-service options available to them through their My Service Canada Account (MSCA): Effective May 28, 2021, individuals may apply online for: an Allowance (ALW) benefit; or an Allowance for the Survivor (ALWS) benefit. Effective June 4, 2021, individuals may apply online for: a Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS) benefit. These new self-serve options will allow individuals to apply for benefits online and to benefit from the unique service delivery capabilities of the online channel. These new options support Service Canada’s commitment to deliver easy to use, seamless, digitally enabled services that put the needs and expectations of Canadians first.

Currently, individuals who want to apply for the Allowance (ALW) or the Allowance for the Survivor (ALWS) benefits can only do so using the paper application form: Application for the Allowance or Allowance for the Survivor - Under the Old Age Security Program (ISP3008). Individuals who want to apply for the Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS) benefit can only do so using: the relevant paper application form: Application for the Guaranteed Income Supplement (ISP3025); or Application for the Guaranteed Income Supplement with Statement of Income (ISP3025B); or the combined OAS pension and GIS benefit online application. Effective May 28, 2021 individuals may apply for the ALW or ALWS benefits and, effective June 4, 2021, individuals may apply for the GIS benefit through their My Service Canada Account (MSCA) secure online portal.

Effective May 28, 2021 and June 4, 2021, new functionality in My Service Canada Account (MSCA) will enable individuals, both those residing within Canada and those residing abroad, to apply for the Allowance (ALW), Allowance for the Survivor (ALWS) or Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS) benefits online. Under the heading OAS/GIS Applications , clients can apply online for an ALW, ALWS or GIS benefit if they meet the conditions that follow. Individuals are eligible to apply online for ALW or ALWS benefits starting May 28, 2021 if they: are between 59+1 month and 65+11 months years of age; though the age for benefit eligibility is between 60 and 64 years of age (including the month of the individual's 65th birthday), individuals can apply 11 months early or, for a retroactive payment, up to 11 months in the past (i.e. back to 65+0 ) ; have no third party representation on file (e.g. Power of attorney, Trustee etc.). Individuals are eligible to apply online for GIS benefit starting June 4, 2021 if they: are age 64+1 month or older; are in pay for an OAS pension or have an OAS pension in Future/Pending status; are not already in pay for the GIS benefit and do not have a GIS benefit in Future/Pending status; and have no third party representation on file (e.g. Power of attorney, Trustee etc.). The online applications for the ALW, ALWS and GIS benefits offer a simplified client experience, asking only relevant questions. This means that clients are only asked questions that are specific to their situation (e.g. applicants born and having always lived in Canada will not be asked to complete the residence question). For ALW and ALWS benefits, clients face a single interface when they start the application. If their spouse or common-law partner is deceased, they receive the ALWS application stream of questions. Otherwise, they receive the ALW stream of questions. When an individual submits an application for the ALW, ALWS or GIS benefits online, based on the individual's home address and marital status, their confirmation page presents: the most applicable proof documentation the individual is required to submit; along with the relevant Service Canada processing centre address to which the individual will send their supporting documentation. Once submitted online, applications for ALW, ALWS or GIS benefits are linked as PDF documents directly to the PWS rather than as a paper form. The application will be processed as per existing processes. A new work item linked to the application is created in PWS and it is assigned it to the applicable processing centre location. Processing agents currently obtain the OAS pension and GIS benefit combined online application work item through Government On Line (GOL) Support Services. This step will no longer be necessary for these new applications because of the direct link from PWS to the ALW/ALWS or GIS benefit online applications. Instead, the PDF applications will be retrieved directly from PWS to be processed as per the existing process for paper applications. There are no actions needed on the part of processing agents to change the status of the application in MSCA. For situations where an applicant does not meet the access rules to apply using MSCA, the system presents an “Unable to continue” page which describes to the applicant the reason(s) why they cannot use this service. The page will offer to the applicant: a link to the Service Canada website for more information; and alternate service channels (e.g. a paper application form).

When an individual is applying online for an ALW benefit, their spouse or common-law partner must provide consent to obtain their information from the Canada Revenue Agency ( CRA ) and declare that the information provided about them is true. The spouse or common-law partner's consent and declaration are considered obtained through their GIS application process if: the details of their marital status match the information provided on the online ALW benefit application you are processing; the CRA Marital Status flag and the CRA Spousal SIN found on the CRA Income ( CRA ) screen in OAS Online, match the information provided, if available; and one of the following conditions are met: both spouses or common-law partners have signed a previously submitted paper OAS / GIS or paper GIS application; the spouse or common-law partner previously submitted an online OAS / GIS or online GIS application and a signed Spousal Consent and Declaration (ISS0954) letter or a Spousal Consent and Declaration GIS (ISS0954A) letter was received; the spouse or common-law partner has been approved for automatic enrolment of the GIS (i.e. the process is not in Pending status); or the spouse or common-law partner has also submitted an online OAS / GIS or online GIS application that is being processed at the same time as the applicant's online ALW benefit application. If there are any discrepancies between the information provided in the spouse or common-law partner's GIS application process, the CRA Income ( CRA ) screen, and the information provided in the online ALW benefit application you are processing affecting eligibility and entitlement, they must be resolved according to regular procedures, before processing the online ALW application. If the spouse or common-law partner's consent and declaration have not been obtained through the GIS application process, this consent can be obtained by sending the Spousal Consent and Declaration ALW (ISS0954B) letter to the spouse or common-law partner to complete. The ISS954B letter allows the spouse or common-law partner to provide: confirmation that the information provided on their behalf is correct; and consent for the Department to request and use their CRA income information to determine their spouse or common-law partner's entitlement for the ALW benefit. If all other eligibility criteria are met, the online application can be approved without the consent and declaration from the spouse or common-law partner; however, the applicant's ALW benefit entitlement cannot be calculated until the consent and declaration are received from the spouse or common-law partner.

Assess hours and predictability of attendance to establish work activity. The following provides a general framework to assess work activity by evaluating hours of work and predictability of attendance. Assess hours and predictablity of attendance Review the file or call the applicant or beneficiary to assess: the actual average hours of work per week they have been able to attend; any workplace accommodations; and their ability to attend work on a regular basis: have their hours changed? have they missed work and why? Assess hours of work When assessing hours of work, it is important to establish actual hours worked versus scheduled hours, as absences due to illness could be disguised through paid leave arrangements such as vacation leave, etc. Do not consider other factors such as availability of work, labour market conditions, or lifestyle choice. While these may result in limited hours, they are not related to the functional limitations from the medical condition. Assess predictability of attendance Determine if their attendance is predictable. The information on file may state that they are scheduled to work a certain number of hours a week (e.g. 29 hours) but if the attendance is unpredictable due to functional limitations from a medical condition, then the hours do not support work activity. Predictability in attendance supports the ability to regularly pursue work. Work activity may be predictable . Below are some indicators to consider when establishing the predictability of work activity: Work or work-like activity may be unpredictable: Assess work activity Determine the presence of work activity: If you cannot establish the presence of work activity, complete a holistic assessment . If you can establish work activity (work hours are predictable), refer to the following guide to view how the hours relate to work capacity: Work activity assessment guidance If work activity hours are: Then: less than 15 hours per week Applicants or beneficiaries participating in paid employment less than 15 hours per week are usually not demonstrating work capacity. Further assessment is required. If work activity hours are: Then: between 15 and 30 hours per week Applicants or beneficiaries participating in paid employment between 15 and 30 hours per week may be demonstrating work capacity. Further assessment is recommended. If work activity hours are: Then: over 30 hours per week Individuals participating in paid employment over 30 hours per week are likely demonstrating work capacity, unless the evidence on file supports otherwise.

Assess w ork activity When you assess the client 's work activity, review the hours spent contributing to the business and the predictability of the client's attendance. This information can be obtained through telephone co ntact with the client and recorded in the Development Call record Calculate the ho urs that the individual contributed to the business including hours spent : producing the product or providing the service; managing the operation of the business; managing and hiring staff; accounting; marketing; scheduling; consulting; maintaining or establishing client relationships; and providing advice and guidance to the business. Ensure the hours worked are predictable and that the individual is able to regularly continue the hours of work. Refer to Severe Criterion—Work Capacity (regular employment, self-employment, seasonal and accommodated) . Severe Criterion—Work Capacity (regular employment, self-employment, seasonal and accommodated) Assess gross business earnings After work activity is established through an assessment of hours and predictability, assess the gross business earnings as follows: Consider the type of business. Calculate the gross business earnings for partnerships or corporations based on the percentage of the individual's share of the business. For example: If the individual is in a partnership with a 40% share of the business, calculate 40% of the gross business earnings as follows: $40,000 gross business earnings multiplied by 40% = $16,000 gross business earnings for the individual. Determine if the individual's gross business earnings are above or below the s ubstantially gainful occupation threshold . When an applicant or beneficiary is working under 30 hours a week, continue the assessment of work capacity by reviewing earnings. Earnings from work activity above the Substantially Gainful Occupation (SGO) level likely indicate work capacity on a predictable basis, unless there is evidence that supports otherwise. Review gross earnings or gross business earnings from work activity for all employment income. For applicants with valid earnings after the Latest Possible Date of Onset (LPDOO) and beneficiaries during a triggered reassessment, check the ITRDS earnings screen. For applicants with a current LPDOO and beneficiaries who report their return to work, obtain their current earnings. Determine if earnings from work activity are above or below SGO benchmark. If earnings are above SGO benchmark: consider that work capacity is likely being demonstrated; and make a decision. If earnings are below SGO benchmark, complete a holistic assessment. The decision should reflect that earnings above the SGO benchmark likely support work capacity, even if the hours are under 15 hours a week. You have established the earnings are from work activity through hours and predictability of attendance. For earnings below the SGO benchmark, consider the following: If the reason is due to: then the likely relation to work capacity is: personal preference; or labour market conditions. unrelated—it is not due to the functional limitations from the medical condition. If the reason is due to: then the likely relation to work capacity is: functional limitations from the medical conditions in combination with: personal characteristics; required treatments; multiple failed work attempts due to functional limitations from the medical conditions; or the nature and progression of the medical conditions. related—it is due to the functional limitations from the medical condition—requires a holistic assessment.

When an applicant or beneficiary has earnings at or above the SGO benchmark amount, these earnings are likely an indicator of work capacity. To ensure these earnings are due to work activity and not other factors, an assessment must be done. This includes an assessment of the: number of hours worked per week; and predictability of attendance. If it is determined that the earnings are not due to work activity, assess the applicant or beneficiary. Severe Criterion—Medical Condition and Functional Limitations (Policy) When a beneficiary is being reassessed retroactively, gaps in the earnings history may be a sign of a failed attempt to return to work. Retroactive reassessment files with up to one calendar year of earnings at or above the SGO benchmark, followed by no earnings in subsequent years, may be treated as a failed attempt to return to work where appropriate and supported by the evidence.

As of November 2019, individuals can apply for the OAS pension or the OAS pension and GIS together online through the My Service Canada Account portal if they: are aged 64 + 1 month or older; are not already in pay or pending for the OAS pension; are a Canadian resident (have no current foreign address on file); and do not have a third party representative (trustee or power of attorney) on file. If any of the above criteria are not met, the applicant will receive a message indicating that they are unable to apply online along with the reason. If all of the above criteria are met, the applicant can complete and submit their application online. Domestic addresses and telephone number updates through the online application are captured directly into ITRDS . When an individual applies online, the information is stored in an internal database within our Department, Government On-Line (GOL) Support Services. An individual can submit multiple online applications for the OAS pension or for the OAS pension and the GIS combined. All submitted applications are stored in the GOL Support Services database indefinitely. The system reads the home postal code the applicant enters and determines where the online application should be sent for processing. The address of the appropriate mail processing centre is recorded in the GOL Support Services database.

Individuals can apply for an OAS pension or income-tested benefit (i.e. GIS, ALW and ALWS benefits) online through the Client Portal on their My Service Canada Account (MSCA) portal if the following conditions are met: When the applicant logs into MSCA and applies for an OAS pension or benefit, the system verifies if a Cúram user account exists. If the system cannot find a match in Cúram, a Prospect Person is created along with a task for the Application Case. If the applicant has an application started in the Client Portal, they can save and exit the application at any time before submitting it. If they attempt to begin another application for the same pension or benefit, they will be prompted to complete the application that is currently in progress. If any of the above criteria are not met for the pension or benefit being applied for, the applicant will be unable to continue and the Apply button will be greyed out. If all of the above criteria are met for the application being applied for, the applicant can complete and submit their application online. Completing and submitting an online application The applicant’s residential and mailing addresses are pre-populated based on information available through MSCA. Any address and telephone number updates made through the online application are captured directly into Cúram and will transfer over to ITRDS . When the applicant submits the application, the information is captured in a date stamped PDF file and the applicant is presented with a confirmation page. For CPP and OAS applications, if the incapacity provision can be applied, the Medical Adjudicator provides the date the last period of continuous incapacity started and the date the incapacity ended, if applicable. In ITRDS , the SCBO will calculate the earlier deemed date of application, if applicable. For CPPD benefits applications, you must determine if: the incapacity provision would be beneficial for the applicant; the requirements of the incapacity provision have been met; and the applicant has or had a "severe and prolonged" disability on or before their latest possible date of onset. If the incapacity provision can be applied, the earlier deemed receipt date of the application is the later of: the month before the 1st month the CPPD benefit could have begun; or the month the last period of continuous incapacity started.

The deemed date of receipt is earlier than the eligibility date The deemed date of receipt of a CPP pension application is more than 11 months after the earliest eligibility date Medically determining the deemed Date of Application for CPPD benefits Diagnosis : chronic vegetative state, meningitis, encephalitis, cavernous sinus thrombosis. March 22, 2016 The applicant was referred to the intensive care unit because the applicant: had a resurgence of fever; had an alteration in mental status and hypotension; failed to regain consciousness; and eventually had to be intubated and ventilated. At the Date of Application (DOA), the applicant remains in a vegetative comatose state without the ability to respond in any way to their environment. The applicant had an acute event resulting in a hospitalization in March 2016. Determination of the deemed DOA The medical evidence shows the applicant became disabled within the meaning of CPP in March 2016. The applicant has been unable to form or express the intent to apply for benefits since March 2016 when they lost consciousness. The incapacity provision allows you to provide a new earlier deemed DOA. The applicant's new earlier deemed DOA is the later of: the month before the first month the relevant benefit could have started to be paid; or the month the applicant's last relevant period of incapacity started. The applicant became disabled in March 2016 and the effective date of payment could have been July 2016. The month before this is June 2016, therefore, the incapacity started in March 2016. The latest of these 2 dates is June 2016. The new deemed DOA is June 2016 and the applicant's disability Date of Onset will be March 2016 with benefits becoming payable in July 2016.

You can view the online application as a PDF file via a link in the Documents section of the PWS work item or the PWS client record. The online application must be processed manually in the same way as a paper application and does not eliminate or replace the paper application. Normal application processing service standards apply.

For more information on the procedures to retrieve and process online applications, refer to the following scenarios: ALW/ALWS Online Application ALW/ALWS Online Application GIS Online Application GIS Online Application An Implementation Bulletin has been developed and can be accessed through a link in the Implementation Bulletin E-Reference Library

The online CPP Survivor's Pension and Child(ren's) Benefits application is available for applicants via My Service Canada Account (MSCA) to apply for an SVR pension and/or children's benefits following the death of a CPP contributor. Existing applicants can log into their MSCA account, while new applicants must register for a MSCA in order to proceed to the online application form. MSCA authenticated clients must agree to the following: Privacy notice for MSCA : Your information is used for the purpose of registering and authenticating yourself before enrolling in various online services accessible through MSCA. Terms of Use for MSCA : You are responsible, accountable and liable for all use and misuse of MSCA associated with your user ID and password. You must use the services provided via MSCA solely for the purposes for which they are offered and for no other purpose, including for no improper or illegal purpose or activity. You must not use MSCA on behalf of anyone else and you must not allow anyone else to use your MSCA. You must access and use MSCA only as yourself. A registered trustee, guardian or other legal representative may act on your behalf in person, by mail or by phone, but not online. The eligibility criteria to apply for an SVR pension and child(ren)’s benefits online are as follows: the applicant must be logged into MSCA and have been authenticated; there must not be a trustee or Power of Attorney on the applicant’s record; the applicant must be a Canadian resident; and the deceased contributor must have made CPP contributions. Leveraging existing MSCA functionalities, applicants have the opportunity to update their address and telephone number with the View and Update Personal Information functionality. Applicants that complete the online CPP Survivor's Pension and Child(ren's) Benefits application must certify that the information is accurate by checking the box provided and submit their application to Service Canada. The electronic signature is captured by ensuring that: the client’s identity is established through their Social Insurance Number; and the client’s intent is established through: their confirmation of the accuracy of the information; and their agreement of the terms and conditions. Immediately following submission, the information entered in MSCA by the applicant is gathered and populated within an electronic PDF version of the online application form. The PDF is then sent to the Digital Repository. The applicant is then directed to a printable confirmation page containing important information such as the timestamp, a list of supporting documents they must mail to Service Canada or a drop off at a nearby Service Canada Centre and the mailing information. Many protective date provisions include a requirement that states that the applicant must have indicated periods of residence or employment under the legislation of the other country on the application for the corresponding pension or benefit. This is known within International Operations as "intent". Depending on the terms of an International Social Security Agreement, intent is e stablished when an applicant: indicates they lived or worked in the other country on their corresponding Canadian pension or benefit application; or requests that the application be considered an application under the legislation of the other country. There are several ways a client can demonstrate intent on a Canadian benefit application. OAS and CPP pension and benefit application forms contain specific fields that question if the applicant has resided or worked in another country. This includ es separate residence statements received during the course of processing, as these statements are considered a part of the application once they have been receive d.

Under certain International Social Security Agreements (ISSA), the only applicable condition is that the client must have applied for the corresponding benefit in the other country. However, most ISSAs will also contain one or more of the following conditions to establish a valid protective date: At the time of application, the applicant must have indicated periods of employment or residence in the other cou ntry (i.e. show ing "intent" on an application). Example An appli cant submits an Application for Canada Pension Plan Disability Benefits (ISP1151) form and indicates a period of residence in the applicable country. The applicant is not required to provide any additional information or details on the application form to satisfy to the conditi on. The applicant requests that the Canadian pension or benefit application be considered an application under the legislation of the other country. Example An applicant submits an Application for the Old Age Security Pension and the Guaranteed Income Supplement (ISP3550) fo rm. On the application, the applicant states that they wish to use the ISP3550 form to also apply for a German retirement pension. The date of receipt of an application for benefits must be after the date of entry into force of the agreement. Example The Canada/Albania ISSA came into force on August 1, 2022. A client applies for an Albanian survivor pension on February 15, 2020, and indicates periods of employment in Canada on the application. Since the Albanian pension application was received before the agreement came into force, it cannot be considered a valid protective date when establishing eligibility to a Canadian SVR pension.

When Canadian pension or benefit rates are requested by a foreign institution, you must provide information for all pensions and benefits in pay, including those that are currently suspended. You must also advise the foreign institution when a Canadian pension or benefit application has been received but is not yet finalized; however, you are not required to place the liaison on hold while awaiting completion of the application. If the foreign institution does not specify from what date they require the rates from, provide the current amounts only. When you are reporting retroactive rates to the foreign institution, report the current rate or rate at the effective date (as required) on the liaison form and attach a record of historical rates.

When sending Canadian pension or benefit information with a foreign benefit application, you must provide all Canadian pension and benefit amounts that the client is receiving and identify those that are currently suspended. You must also advise the foreign institution when a Canadian pension or benefit application has been received but is not yet finalized; however, you are not required to place the liaison on hold while awaiting completion of the application. Each country outlines the Canadian pension or benefit information you must provide to the responsible foreign institution along with a foreign benefit application. You may be required to provide: the current rate of payment; the rate from a specific date; or the rate from the effective date.

As part of the Economic and Fiscal Update 2021 , the Government announced it would provide a one-time, non-taxable grant to alleviate financial hardship of Guaranteed Income Supplement ( GIS ) and Allowance ( ALW ) recipients who received pandemic benefits in 2020. Economic and Fiscal Update 2021 In July 2021, some GIS and ALW /Allowance for the Survivor recipients experienced a reduction or loss of benefits because of receiving pandemic payments in 2020. The amount of an individual's grant payment varied and corresponded to the annualized amount of their reduction or loss in GIS / ALW benefits. The recipient's monthly benefit loss was determined by comparing the maximum monthly reduction of GIS / ALW payments between June 2021 and July 2021 using March 2022 data. Once the maximum monthly reduction was established, the amount was multiplied by 12. The one-time grant was equal to the total 12-month reduction or loss of the GIS or ALW monthly payment amount. The grant payment was issued automatically in April 2022, and without the need for an application. Some grant payments were issued manually for dire need situations in March 2022 and some grant payments were issued between May 2022 and March 2023 for individuals who would become retroactively entitled to it. The one-time grant was not an OAS payment; it was issued under separate authorities. Eligibility To be entitled for the grant payment, individuals must have been eligible for the GIS or an GIS / ALW as of March 2022. These individuals must also have: received (or had a spouse/common-law partner who received) a "pandemic benefit" in 2020. A pandemic benefit is defined as one of the following benefits: the Canada Emergency Response Benefit; the Employment Insurance Emergency Response Benefit; the Canada Recovery Benefit; the Canada Recovery Sickness Benefit; or the Canada Recovery Caregiving Benefit. been in receipt of GIS and ALW benefits in June 2021 (or received a GIS and an ALW benefit in respect of June 2021); and experienced a reduction or loss in GIS and ALW benefits in July 2021. One-time grant details Overpayments Any overpaid grant payments may be reviewed under existing departmental collection policies. The Department will not attempt to recover the one-time grant payment from an estate when the GIS and ALW recipient dies before March 2022, but the Department is only notified after issuing the one-time grant payment. Agents are not required to calculate the amount of the grant payment, nor to validate the amount. If you come across a situation where you believe an overpayment may have occurred because you have reason to believe the client did not meet the eligibility criteria, send an enquiry via the Business Expertise Request Tool by following normal channels for next steps. Business Expertise Request Tool Return of payment If a GIS and ALW recipient does not wish to receive the grant payment, they may be directed to write a cheque payable to the Receiver General for Canada, or donate it to a charity of their choice. The pensioner must include a covering note, which should include their Social Insurance Number, name, contact information and the reason for returning the payment. The payment must be returned as follows: Direction The pensioner should write a cheque payable to the Receiver General for Canada and include the following information on the cheque their full name; their Social Insurance Number; the statement: One-Time Grant for GIS Recipients Who Received Pandemic Benefits. Pensioners can either: mail the cheque to the following address: ESDC -National Accounts Receivable 100-1081 Main Street Moncton, NB E1C 1H1; or bring the cheque with the covering note to any Service Canada Centre. Direction Attach the paper cheque to the covering note; Pensioners can either: mail it to the following address: Cheque Redemption and Control Directorate-Returned Cheques P.O. Box 2000 Matane, QC G4W 4N5; or bring the covering note and paper cheque to any Service Canada Centre.
