The DSB and the PRDB are separate benefits. Each has its own eligibility requirements. Eligibility Requirements— PRDB (Policy)

If the applicant meets the non-medical eligibility requirements for both the DSB and PRDB at the time of the initial adjudication, each decision regarding the DSB and PRDB entitlement must be clearly communicated separately in the decision letter. The applicant has the right to request a reconsideration of each decision, either together or separately.

If the applicant meets the non-medical eligibility requirements for both the DSB and PRDB at the time of the initial adjudication, each decision (i.e. DSB entitlement, PRDB entitlement) and its corresponding appeal rights must be communicated independently in the decision letter to the applicant. The applicant has the right to request a reconsideration of each decision either together or separately.

Unlike the medical adjudication for a DSB , the Latest Possible Date of Onset for the medical adjudication for a PRDB will either be the month of the applicant’s 65th birthday, or May 4, 2023, which is the day prior to the amended legislation coming into force. For the PRDB , medical adjudication is to: determine if the applicant has a severe and prolonged disability as per the CPP; and establish a date on which the individual became disabled. The DOO for a PRDB cannot be earlier than: 15 months prior to the date of application; the effective date of the early CPP RTR pension; or January 2019. It is not necessary for the DOO or established DOO to be within the Minimum Qualifying Period (MQP) and can be outside of the MQP.

The purpose of medical adjudication is to: determine if the applicant has a severe and prolonged disability as per the CPP; and determine a Date of Onset (DOO). Regular PRDB applications To be eligible for the PRDB , the applicant must be found to be disabled on or before their Latest Possible Date of Onset (LPDOO) and their ERTR pension effective date must fall on or before their LPDOO. The DOO for the PRDB : must be on or before their LPDOO; cannot be earlier than the month of the applicant's ERTR pension effective date; can be up to 15 months before the receipt date of the DSB or PRDB application; and cannot be earlier than May 2023. Late PRDB applications The 3 following criteria must be met before a determination of severe and prolonged can occur: the applicant must have sufficient CPP contributions to establish an LPDOO; the LPDOO must be after April 30, 2023; and the effective date of the applicant's ERTR pension must fall before the LPDOO. Regardless of when their disability began, the applicant must be found to be disabled on or before their LPDOO and continue to meet the severe and prolonged CPPD criteria into the future. The applicant's established DOO must be: on or after the month of the effective date of their ERTR pension; after April 30, 2023; and on or before their LPDOO. The DOO for the PRDB cannot be: more than 15 months before the receipt date of the PRDB application; and earlier than May 2023 .

If the DOO or established DOO falls in May 2023, send these cases to National Headquarters via the Business Expertise Request Tool. In order to be eligible for the PRDB , the applicant must: be in receipt of their Early Retirement (ERTR) pension; have a contributory period; and be determined to be disabled as per the CPP. Refer to Non-Medical Eligibility—CPPD Benefits (Policy) January 2019. Non-Medical Eligibility—CPPD Benefits (Policy)

If the DOO or established DOO falls in May 2023, send these cases to National Headquarters via the Business Expertise Request Tool. The purpose of the PRDB is to provide protection to CPP RTR pensioners who have: been in pay for an Early Retirement (ERTR) pension for 15 months or more and have become disabled; or become disabled after starting to receive their ERTR pension. To be eligible for the PRDB , the applicant must: be in receipt of their ERTR; meet the contributory requirements; and be determined to be disabled within the meaning of the CPP. Refer to Non-Medical Eligibility—CPPD Benefits (Policy) May 5, 2023. Non-Medical Eligibility—CPPD Benefits (Policy)

The DSB and the PRDB are distinct benefits that require separate decisions at each level of adjudication. If the initial decision is only regarding eligibility for a DSB , the reconsideration request only applies to the DSB determination. In the case where both benefits are denied, the applicant can decide to request one or both decisions to be reconsidered together or separately. It is important to understand which decision the reconsideration request is related to, either the DSB , PRDB or both. If the applicant was not in pay for an ERTR pension at the time of the initial decision but is in pay at the time of the reconsideration, an Application for a Canada Pension Plan Post-Retirement Disability Benefit (ISP1170) form is required from the applicant before the adjudication of a PRDB at the initial level can occur. This decision will have its own reconsideration rights. It is possible in some cases that the DSB and PRDB applications may be at different appeal levels. Reconsideration (Policy)

The DSB and the PRDB are distinct benefits that require separate decisions at each level of adjudication. If the initial decision is only regarding eligibility for a DSB , the reconsideration request only applies to the DSB determination. In cases where both benefits are denied, the applicant can decide to request a reconsideration of one or both decisions together or separately. It is important to understand which decision the applicant's reconsideration request is related to: the DSB ; the PRDB ; or both. If the applicant was not in pay for an Early Retirement (ERTR) pension at the time of the initial decision, but the ERTR pension is in pay at the time of the reconsideration, the applicant must provide a completed, signed and dated Application for a Canada Pension Plan Post-Retirement Disability Benefit (ISP1170) form before the adjudication of a PRDB at the initial level can occur. The PRDB application decision will have its own reconsideration rights. It is possible that in some cases, the DSB and the PRDB applications may be at different appeal levels. Reconsideration (Policy)

There are no transitional provisions in the legislation. Therefore, eligibility decisions must be made in alignment with the law in effect regardless of when the application was received. The DSB and the PRDB are distinct benefits. They require separate decisions which must be communicated at each level of adjudication. If the applicant starts to receive an Early Retirement pension at any time after the initial DSB decision is made and the application remains active, an Application for a Canada Pension Plan Post-Retirement Disability Benefit (ISP1170) form may be sent. The application remains active when there is a request for reconsideration or an appeal to the SST . A discrepancy report is generated to compare clients' marital status on file with the Department against their marital status reported to the CRA and identifies accounts with discrepancies. In June 2022, the Benefits and Integrated Services Branch (BISB) collaborated with the Integrity Services Branch (ISB) to review the discrepancy report that originally identified nearly 26,000 clients with a marital status discrepancy. In October 2022, the review concluded that 16,000 clients who receive GIS self-reported changes in marital status to the Department between June and October. ISB has been reviewing a selected group of accounts. During the week of March 20, 2023, a Marital Status Questionnaire (ISP-3152) letter was sent to clients included on this report. These accounts are identified by the following automated ITRDS notes: For accounts under review with ISB: ISB CRA/GIS Marital Status Review – account under review with ISB For accounts included in the mail-out by BISB: Client included in the BISB CRA marital status discrepancy mailing. Refer to KA-05166 Clients who receive the ISP-3152 letter must complete the Marital Status Questionnaire section and return it to the Department. The marital status on file with the Department is listed on the first page of the ISP-3152 letter. If the client is indicating a marital status that is different from what is currently on file with the Department, they must include a copy of any supporting documentation, such as a marriage certificate or death certificate. If a response was not received, a Marital Status Questionnaire - reminder letter (ISP-3152B) was automatically sent in June 2023 and an additional Marital Status Questionnaire - reminder letter (ISP-3152C) was sent on January 12, 2024. Both letters advised the clients their benefits may be suspended if no response is received. If the client fails to respond to the requests, National Headquarters will create an Account Verification work item in PWS with the barcode NHQ-OASMSD23-REMIND for processing. If a client has not responded to written requests for information, you must make reasonable efforts to contact them. When all attempts to contact them and obtain the required information have failed, determine if the client has failed to respond, is non-compliant or if their whereabouts are unknown and suspend the applicable benefits. Whereabouts unknown New A client's whereabouts are unknown if: they have not responded to written requests for information or attempts to contact them by phone; and there is no indication on file that the current address has changed; or correspondence has been returned by Canada Post as undeliverable. If a client's whereabouts are unknown, you must suspend their OAS and income-tested benefits and notify CPP and International Operations. Failure to Respond and Non-compliance New A client fails to respond if: they received correspondence from the Department but did not respond; you determine there is an indication on file (other correspondence, recent contact by phone, or cashed cheques) that the current address is correct; and their whereabouts are not in question. A client is non-compliant if: they respond but refuse to provide the requested information. If a client fails to respond or is non-compliant, you must suspend their income tested benefits until the requested information is received. For more information regarding the suspension of benefits, Suspension (Policy) It is important to add the required notes to ITRDS exactly as described so that these accounts can be identified for future review.

The change to IO is centered around the naming protocols within PWS. Before February 6, 2023 IO work was identified 2 ways: by virtue of the processing centre location (IO WT or IO ATL) and as well, by the Program or Category choices. This required all work involving IO to have changes made to the Program or Category in addition to the Location . Errors result when we see IO named work in domestic processing locations and domestic-named work in IO locations. Although these errors may be just the failure to adjust the Program or Category , it required investigation and correction to either Program and Category , or Location . Rather than having 2 ways to identify IO work, this change focuses on defining IO work items as work which is located in the IO processing centres (IO WT and IO ATL). IO work items will now use the same naming protocols that exist for domestic inventory, and no adjustments to the Program or Category will be required when work items moves to and from IO. Overall, this simplifies the PWS entries for work movement. Before February 6, 2023, there were 4 program choices: CPP, DSB, OAS and IO. The IO program will no longer exist; however, the Foreign Benefits program will be a selection as there is no domestic equivalent for Foreign Benefits. The number of categories will reduce from 14 to 3.

As of February 6, 2023, the following changes specifically related to International Operations (IO) will be implemented in PWS. The IO program will no longer exist; rather IO inventory will be represented by outstanding work items in the processing location International Operations – ATL (IO ATL) or International Operations – WT (IO WT). The Program and Category will match the domestic fields within IO WT and IO ATL locations. The Foreign Benefit program will exist for all Foreign Benefit work, with the Category of Applications or Maintenance. The Country of Agreement field will appear on all work types, both domestic and international, and should continue to be used when work is moved to the IO ATL and IO WT processing locations. An IO Service Standard and age counter will be available on the Work Item details screen.

All current IO work items will use the same naming protocols that exist for domestic inventory, and no adjustments to Program or Category will be required when work moves to and from IO. Overall, this simplifies the PWS entries for work movement. As such, it is critical for IO work to be created in or moved to the correct processing location, being IO WT or IO ATL. In addition, all outstanding IO work items (excluding completed or deleted work items) will change to the existing domestic program and category. All new work received on or after February 6 , 2023 will be loaded using the new naming protocols. The PWS processing location will determine if the work item is within domestic inventories or IO inventory. A new program has been created for Foreign Benefits related work with matching categories of Applications and Maintenance. The location on these work items should be one of the 2 IO locations, i.e. IO WT or IO ATL. Because the domestic and international naming aligns, the Country of Agreement field appears on all work items and is no longer a mandatory PWS field. For work moving to IO, the Country of Agreement needs to be completed as this field determines the correct IO location. Once completed, the Country of Agreement remains on the work item even if moved back to a domestic processing location. An IO service standard and age counter (days spent in an IO location) will appear on the Work Item details screen in addition to the domestic service standard and age counter. This will appear when a work item is created in or moved to an IO location. The IO clock remains on the Work Item details screen even if the work item moves back to a domestic location, and the IO age counter stops when the work item is in a domestic location. This change supports call centres and in-person with a more fulsome understanding of the client’s submission and where they are situated in terms of processing timeframes. Procedures provide CPP, OAS and International Operations staff with guidance for correcting accounts where a discrepancy exists between programs concerning a client’s biographical dates. Discrepancies may exist when the Date of Birth (DOB) or Date of Death (DOD) in 2 or more programs do not match, or when the DOD is only recorded in one program (CPP, for example) while another program’s benefits (OAS, for example) are still In Pay .

In Cúram, Canadian residence periods in an FEC are used to capture Canadian residence that was reported to a foreign country on a liaison. You can add, view, edit or delete Canadian residence periods in the Evidence tab of the FEC for the applicable country. After a Canadian residence period is added, changed or deleted, it must be activated in Cúram before it can be used to adjudicate OAS/CPP applications under a Social Security Agreement. There are no limits to how many entries you can make and how many gaps in residence periods are allowed. If a Canadian residence period overlaps with a foreign contribution period, an issue will be raised on the Evidence Dashboard. This must be resolved before the evidence can be activated. Residence Period—Add, View and Edit in Cúram (Action) Each Canadian residence period can have multiple statuses, as indicated by the icons below.

If a contribution period and a Canadian residence period overlap, an issue will be raised in Cúram. When activating either period, you will be prompted to resolve the issue. The issue will always need to be resolved on the Canadian residence period. Once it has been resolved, you will need to reactivate the period. If you add an overlapping contribution period after the Canadian residence period has already been activated, you will need to resolve the issue from Active Evidence in the page group navigation bar. If you add an overlapping Canadian residence period after the contribution period has already been activated, you will need to resolve the issue from In Edit Evidence in the page group navigation bar.

PEP functionality allows you to manually enter account information required to adjudicate CPP benefits. This process allows you to bypass certain programming issues and legislative limitations found in ITRDS . Before data capturing the PEP block, you must review the client's account to ensure it is complete and correct. You must also manually calculate the client's RTR -FBC and entitlement period using the Canada Pension Plan Calculation Module or the ITRDS Simulation functionality. It takes 2 users to request and approve a PEP data capture: the Requester who creates a new PEP request and sends it for approval; and the Approver who verifies information captured in the PEP block. Once verified, they will either approve the request or return the request to the Requester for modification.

The Program Exception Process (PEP) system is used to bypass certain calculations that would normally be done in ITRDS, specifically the calculation of the Retirement For Benefit Calculation (RTR-FBC). Authorized users can enter a manually calculated RTR-FBC into the PEP block. PEP then uses the manually entered RTR-FBC and other benefit information to calculate the benefit amount. PEP has built in rules that prevent the user from entering an amount free of benefit adjudication rules. In other words, the user cannot enter any amount to be paid. The Canada Pension Plan Calculation Module (CPPCM) is primarily used to calculate the RTR-FBC amount. The reasons for which a user would enter a manually calculated RTR-FBC (to override the automatically calculated one) would include but not limited to: ITRDS system bugs or a ministerial decision. While PEP is a suitable platform to pay most accounts that can’t be paid in ITRDS, it does have certain limitations. If there is a system bug that affects both ITRDS and PEP, the agent must issue a manual priority payment to pay the benefit.

Cúram connects with the Corporate Correspondence Tool (CCT) to create and reprint correspondence. Create Correspondence This process begins when you need to create correspondence, a letter, to communicate with a client or a third party. The letter is generated based on a template in the CCT. When creating correspondence in Cúram, the system will automatically open CCT in your browser. Creating correspondence can be done on a Person’s profile or on a Foreign Engagement Case (FEC). When correspondence is specific to an FEC, you must add it to the case. All the correspondence will display on the Person’s profile, but only the correspondence specific to an FEC will display on the case. The system automatically retrieves communication details for correspondence previously registered in Cúram (e.g. mailing address and preferred language). These must already have been created on the Person’s profile for the correspondence to be created. Cúram assigns a unique Correspondence Tracking Number for every correspondence created. The Correspondence Tracking Number hyperlink will only be enabled if the Communication Status is Sent , Returned or Void . Once enabled, the hyperlink will allow you to view the CCT letter. Unverified Contact for A Deceased Person You must remove a deceased person’s information in the Date of Death , Date Notified of Death and Country of Death fields under Birth and Death Details in the Evidence tab before adding an unverified contact if you are required to send correspondence to the unverified contact. Once the correspondence is sent, you must add back the information you removed. Manage a Person’s Record in Cúram (Action) Reprint Correspondence The process for reprinting correspondence begins when a client calls and requests a copy of their letter. This involves 2 steps: downloading the original letter and then uploading it to the new correspondence. Reprinting is only possible when the correspondence status is set to Returned , Void , or Sent in Cúram. There are 2 types of cover letters available: one for letter format and one for legal format.

Correspondence (i.e. letters) are created in Cúram to communicate with a client or a verified third party on a Person record, Application Case, Integrated Case and/or a Foreign Engagement Case. If you cannot find the correspondence template in Cúram, updated versions are available on the Forms and Letters page of the KMT. You must search for NATS letters temporarily stored on the KMT before searching in NATS. There are 3 types of letters being generated out of Cúram with the Corporate Correspondence Tool (CCT): bulk letters; on demand letters; and manual letters. For every letter created (bulk, on demand or manual), a correspondence tracking number and a communication record is created in Cúram. All correspondence is displayed on the Person record, but only the correspondence specific to a case are created and displayed on the Case record. To create a letter, you must specify the recipients of the correspondence, select a template to use, and complete all mandatory data/selections and/or all required options. A pop-up interface with the CCT is used to complete the template and generate the correspondence. Refer to Confirmed Priority ISS Template Titles – 2024-07-17 (Excel, 44 KB) Download link for a current list of available templates. Confirmed Priority ISS Template Titles – 2024-07-17 Once the correspondence template has been opened, a hyperlink is created based on the correspondence tracking number and work item generated for that letter. If required, you can submit an incomplete application to enable you to generate correspondence from the Application Case.

Design improvements have been divided into the following categories: Automatic enrollment improvements Automatic enrollment improvements Automation improvements Automation improvements Financial improvements Financial improvements User experience improvements User experience improvements Client experience improvements Client experience improvements Workload improvements Workload improvements Return to Automatic enrollment improvements Person-matching logic improvements The automatic enrolment matching logic has been simplified to consider a match when a verified SIN and date of birth (year and month only) match that of an existing registered or prospect person. In the case of the prospect person, the system will convert the prospect to registered. The same logic will be applied to the GIS automatic enrolment spousal matching. This will significantly reduce the exclusions from automatic enrolment. Exclusion reasons have been updated for better clarity. Daily authorization for automatic enrolment Application Cases (OAS pension and GIS) The automatic enrolment authorization job now runs daily from the 1st to the 15th day of the month and only authorizes the Application Cases on the day the client turns 65. This will significantly reduce the number of manual interventions necessary when a client opts out of automatic enrolment before their birthday after the 1st day of the month. Return to Automation improvements Management of ALW benefit and ALWS benefit conversions Conversions no longer require manual investigation in most cases. Benefits of clients who meet the 40‑year residency requirement will convert more quickly, improving client service and legislative compliance. Only exceptional cases will generate follow‑up tasks, while the majority of cases will be handled seamlessly through automated processing. Automated death notification process Officers will receive exception workloads automatically. Manual reports or ad hoc tasks will no longer be created. This automation ensures: faster, consistent handling of Date of Death (DOD) cases; clear auditability; the proactive mailing of correct correspondence; improved client service for surviving spouses; and a reduced risk of missed actions when DOD changes are received from ITRDS. Return to Financial improvements Prevention of the payment of aged and low-value amounts Officers no longer need to track or cancel small and aged underpayments. The system will automatically accrue these amounts and include them in the next payment once they exceed the payment threshold. If the threshold is not reached, the amounts will continue to accrue for up to 12 months, after which they will be paid to the client. Clients will not see outdated, low‑value amounts merged into future payments, which will reduce incorrect payments and improve accuracy. This automation: ensures compliance with legislative requirements; improves client service; and improves financial integrity across programs. Inbound garnishment from the Department of Justice This improvement eliminates the creation of duplicate garnishment deductions on a client's file, reducing the number of financial inaccuracies that require manual intervention by officers. This fix will ensure that modified Department of Justice instructions replace existing deductions, instead of duplicating them. Liability offsets coded as a reversible deduction Officers no longer need to fix incorrect offsets or reconcile unwanted non‑reversible deductions after cancellations. Financial records, Year to Date amounts, and tax slip data will remain accurate because the system will correctly categorize and reprocess cancelled offsets. This improvement: reduces financial reporting errors; prevents incorrect recoveries from clients; and supports correct handling during reissue or reconcile‑and‑reissue workflows. In support of this release, the Integrated Expertise Network has developed a Liability Offset job aid that explains how: to apply a liability offset; to understand system generated activation tasks; offsets are reversed when a payment is cancelled in the Standard Payment System (SPS); and to manage cancelled payments with a liability offset previously applied. For additional information, refer to the Job Aids SharePoint link section of the ESDC’s Cúram SharePoint site. Job Aids Return to User experience improvements Evidence Correction task logic to reduce occurrences of 201 tasks and Awaiting Resolution statuses on Application Cases Officers will receive fewer Evidence Correction tasks, allowing: officers to process applications faster with less back‑and‑forth; workload managers to gain more predictable workflow, with fewer stalled tasks and clearer prioritization; and clients to experience quicker processing timelines, fewer callbacks, and a reduced risk of repeated contact for missing information. Historic Recalculation Data from the Recalculation (CAL) screen Officers can now: reference historical entitlement information to assist them in resolving client enquiries using complete legacy account data; access monthly details which will reduce errors, prevent payment delays, and support accurate manual recalculations; and immediately access the information they need, without triggering system rules or unintended changes. Return to Client experience improvements Client portal style guidelines improvements Clients will experience a more consistent, accessible, and user‑friendly interface throughout the online application process. Pages will look and behave predictably across the portal, reducing confusion and helping clients complete applications more easily. These improvements strengthen usability, accessibility, and overall trust in the digital experience. Client portal application improvements Clients will experience a smoother, more intuitive application flow with related questions grouped together and presented in a logical order. The process is easier to understand, reducing confusion and improving completion success. Behind the scenes, the system will use newly collected data to support accurate application intake and eligibility and entitlement decisions. Return to Workload improvements General task changes Tasks are now easier to read, locate, and manage. The tasks have clearer information, new tasks fields and enhanced search capabilities which improves allocation, monitoring, and overall workflow efficiency. There are 11 new on hold reasons and 12 new deferred reasons available for users to select for tasks. Each new task has its own reason and a Bring Forward date assigned to it. When users: change a task’s status to On-Hold , they must also select the appropriate work queue that the on hold task must be assigned to. select a new deferred task, they must keep it in their own work queue for further action. The On Hold and Deferred Reason Code Descriptions SharePoint link list is available on the ESDC's Cúram SharePoint site. On Hold and Deferred Reason Code Descriptions The system will automatically capture who closed a task, providing better auditability. These improvements optimize workload management and streamline daily operations across all programs. Capture communications for deceased records Officers can now accurately capture communications from clients who incorrectly appear deceased in the system and who present themselves in person to correct the record. The validation error will no longer prevent communication entry, improving accuracy and client service. This ensures smoother correction of erroneous death notifications and supports proper case management. The PRDB legislation enacted in 2019 did not align with the contributory requirements of the DSB . It did not have a reference to “wholly or partly within a contributory period” which meant proration could not be considered. The 2019 legislation did not provide for exclusions (i.e. Child Rearing Provision and previous periods of disability) when determining the MQP. The recent legislative change on May 5, 2023, now aligns the contributory requirements for the PRDB with those of the DSB .

On May 5, 2023, Bill C-19, which includes new legislation for the PRDB , came into effect. This legislative change realigns the contributory requirements for the PRDB with those of the DSB . The exception being that PRB earnings are also to be considered in the determination of the PRDB minimum qualifying period (MQP).

Deactivated Work Types Upon implementation of the terminal application definition change no additional work items will be able to be created using the following work types: Medical Report/Information - Terminal Illness Medical Report/Information Grave Condition Once existing work items have been completed these work types will be deactivated. New Triage and Description Fields New triage fields have been added to the Disability (1151) Application and the Medical Report (2519) work types. The following drop-down options will be available to indicate if the work item has been triaged: No Yes The field will default to No . Regions choosing to have 2 levels of review (i.e. initially reviewed by the Program Support Clerk (PSC) with a second review by the Medical Adjudicator (MA)), must not update the triage field to Yes until the second review has occurred. Instead, other existing fields within the work item should be used to refer the work item for secondary triage i.e. the complexity field (MA-1). The triage field is not being added to the Medical Report - Terminal Illness (2530B) work type as this automatically classifies the application as a Terminal application. A description field is being added to the Medical Report (2519) work type. The following description drop-down options will be available: Terminal Illness Grave Condition Regular The field will default to Regular . Once the Medical Report for Canada Pension Plan Disability Benefits (ISP-2519) form has been triaged the description field in PWS must be updated to reflect the medical report classification: Where Section 4 indicates that the client's medical condition is Terminal select Terminal Illness in the description field. Where Section 4 or the Medical Report indicates that the client's medical condition is Grave select Grave Condition in the description field. Keep the description field as Regular for all other medical conditions where Section 4 is blank and the Medical Report does not indicate a Grave Condition. Where a Disability Application and Medical Report are triaged simultaneously it is necessary to update the triage fields on both the Application and the Medical Report and update the description field on the Medical Report. The application work type should be changed to Disability – Terminal Illness, Disability - Grave Condition, or Disability (1151) as appropriate.

Before registering a prospect person, you must search and verify if the record already exists in Cúram. Search for a Person in Cúram (Action) There are 2 scenarios to register a prospect person in Cúram: If the paper application form or correspondence that a client sends is missing mandatory information to register the client as a person, you can register the client as a prospect person. The mandatory information includes: First Name Last Name Date of Birth Preferred communication language Residential and mailing addresses In International Operations, the Foreign Engagement Case country is one of the 3 restricted countries (the United States, Japan, and Jamaica), and liaisons, foreign benefit decisions, and/or documentations are received directly from one of those countries' foreign institutions. In these instances, you may need to send a correspondence requesting the missing mandatory information from the prospect person, if necessary. Correspondence—Create, Update, and Check Status in Cúram (Action) If a prospect person applies for an OAS pension or benefit, you must convert the prospect person to a person in Cúram first. You may need to send correspondence requesting the missing information from the prospect person, if necessary. Register a Prospect Person as a Person in Cúram (Action) If you have the SIN, reference number or correspondence tracking number, refer to the Search for a Prospect Person using Search Criteria section in the What you need to do section of the Step by Step tab. If you do not have any reference number or correspondence tracking number, refer to the Search for a Prospect Person using Additional Search Criteria section in the What you need to do section of the Step by Step tab.

Before registering a prospect person as a person, you must search and verify that the prospect person record exists in Cúram. Search for a Person in Cúram (Action) There are 3 scenarios to convert a prospect person to a person in Cúram: If an individual was created as a prospect person, and sufficient information is later obtained to register the individual as a person, you need to convert the prospect person profile to a person profile. If an individual was created as a prospect person because their information was received directly from a restricted International Social Security Agreement country and all the information becomes available from a non-restricted source (e.g. the client provides an application for Canadian benefits, an application for foreign benefits is received from a non-restricted country or a non-restricted foreign country provides the client’s information), you need to convert the prospect person profile to a person profile. If a prospect person applies for an OAS pension or benefit, you must first convert the prospect person to a person in Cúram. You may need to send correspondence requesting the missing information from the prospect person, if necessary. Refer to Correspondence—Create, Update, and Check Status in Cúram (Action) . This procedure provides you with the steps to reallocate an overpayment due to misrepresentation or fraud and write it off from a client's account in Cúram when an investigation by the Integrity Services Branch (ISB) determined that it occurred due to misrepresentation or fraud by a third party.

Overpayments made to a client receiving an OAS pension or benefits are processed as liabilities against the client and are considered debts that must be repaid. An investigation by ISB may determine that an overpayment assigned to a client is a result of a misrepresentation or fraud by a third party. In this case the person who committed the fraud or misrepresentation is liable for the debt, not the client. When a notification of misrepresentation or fraud is received, you must reallocate the overpayment to the account of the person who committed the fraud or misrepresentation and write-off (i.e. reduce) the overpayment on the original client's account in Cúram.

A client's entitlements under OAS program are governed by rules that have been programmed into the Cúram system. Cúram will automatically reassess entitlement when evidence is activated following its addition or modification. If automatic reassessment does not complete, the reassessment can be triggered manually.

Cúram will automatically recalculate a client's entitlement when new information is added or when existing information is updated and activated. If this automatic recalculation does not go through, staff can start the reassessment manually. For more information, Manually Reassess Entitlement in Cúram (Action)

Cash Receipts refer to money received in Employment and Social Development Canada to apply towards departmental debts that are managed in Public Sector Collections and Disbursements (PSCD). Normally this money is received either via online banking, cheques or through cross program deductions. Cash receipts are stored under the Financials tab under a person profile or overpayment case in Cúram. When PSCD receives payments to apply against a client's liability, the payment details are sent to Cúram to be stored as a cash receipt. This is the same process involved when PSCD receives cross program liability payments from CPP towards an OAS debt. Cash receipts are generated by the system, and Cúram will record the cash receipt under the user's profile while automatically reducing the outstanding balance of the liability. Additionally, PSCD can send a Cash Receipt Reversal to Cúram to reverse a previously sent cash receipt. Cúram will process this information and add the cash receipt amount back to the outstanding balance of the liability. The cash receipt table displays specific details about the payment. The Method column indicates the source from which the amount was received. The Amount column shows the total payment received. The PSCD Details and Allocations sections are located below the main table. These sections can be expanded by clicking the ( > ) toggle icon next to each section. The Allocations section displays the liability to which the payment was allocated towards, along with the respective dollar amount.

The Public Sector Collections and Disbursements (PSCD) system can send a reversal of a cash payment to Cúram. When this happens, Cúram uses a Payment Received Reversal functionality to record and display the reversal. This cancels the corresponding received payment and creates a reversal record for tracking purposes. A cash receipt reversal also updates the outstanding balances on the overpayment that was updated by that payment when it was initially created. The Cash Received amount previously received is added back to the Departmental Liability outstanding balance. Cash receipt reversal is automatic. The procedure in this document is only necessary when the automated procedure fails. The cash receipt reversal received from PSCD and applied to the applicable overpayment in Cúram will generate a task containing the following information: Client SIN or Cúram reference number Client name Total overpayment amount Date Product delivery case type Product delivery case reference number Overpayment authorization requirement In addition, the task may indicate one of the following: That overpayment letters will be sent That the case needs to be reviewed That the overpayment penalties or interests can be applied to offset an underpayment PSCD will only send one reversal for a cash receipt. The cash receipt will be indicated by its SAP document number. Cúram will reverse all transactions associated with the document number. The principal amount and the interest owed initially communicated by PSCD may be different at the time the reversal is sent. Cúram will reverse both the principal and the interest amounts. For example, if the principal and interest amounts sent for the cash receipt received were different, PSCD will send a reversal of the cash receipt received. Based on the SAP document number, Cúram will reverse both the principal (overpayment) and interest amounts.

In Cúram, you can add third party contacts as either an Individual or an External Party organization. In either case, a profile is created to manage the third party contact information (e.g. direct deposit information, address, phone number). To add or modify a third party representative's financial information, Third Party Direct Deposit Information—Add, View and Edit in Cúram (Action) To modify a third party representative's contact information, Register a Third-Party Organization, Office and Office Member in Cúram (Action) All External Third Party organizations must be registered before they can be added as a third party contact. If they are not registered, refer to Register a Third-Party Organization, Office and Office Member in Cúram (Action) before proceeding. Register a Third-Party Organization, Office and Office Member in Cúram (Action) Certain role types are eligible to be assigned as the case nominee. For more information, Manage Payment Destination for Nominees—Add, Edit and View in Cúram (Action) Once you add a verified third party contact, Cúram allows you to send correspondence to them directly. When you add verified third party contacts, you must always ensure that proper documentation is received. In rare cases, a client can have an unverified third party contact. For example, if a client dies or becomes incapable, insufficient documentation may be received by an unverified third party. In such cases where further documentation is required to verify the contact or additional communication is necessary, you must create an unverified contact to communicate with the unverified individual. Unverified Contacts—Add, Edit, and Cancel in Cúram (Action) After you create a Third Party Contact evidence, you can only modify the Third Party Correspondence field, as well as the From and To date fields. The Program , Role , Role Type , Language Preference and Relationship to client fields cannot be modified. The only third party information sent to ITRDS is the Third Party Contact evidence with the role of Representative . This occurs only if CPP is checked in the Program box for the Third Party Contact evidence.

An OAS / GIS Application Case is automatically created once an OAS and GIS application form is added in Cúram. Add an OAS and GIS Application Form in Cúram (Action) An OAS / GIS Application Case can be accessed from the person's profile. You can view the OAS / GIS application for more information associated with a client's Application before starting the authorizing process. If a client's OAS application was approved before the cutover (i.e. before March 1, 2025) but their GIS application was not, you must submit a standalone “Application for Guaranteed Income Supplement” to authorize the GIS . However, if you submit a new “Application for Old Age Security Pension and Guaranteed Income Supplement” instead, you must proceed with completing all necessary case work in the Application Case, including adding evidences, completing verifications, and resolving any outstanding tasks. The OAS benefit should then be authorized. Cúram will copy the relevant evidence to the migrated Integrated Case. You must then review the Integrated Case to ensure all evidence has been carried over to the Integrated Case and determine whether any overrides need to the updated or removed based on the information available. You can now authorize the GIS . After the OAS pension has been authorized, the Benefits page refreshes automatically and updates the status of the Benefit from Pending to Approved , and Completed On date is populated. The application case status is changed to Closed. Before authorizing your application case you can click Check Eligibility, Cúram runs eligibility checks and updates the eligibility decision on the eligibility check screen. You can view the details of the unmet criteria (e.g. residency, age) on the potential eligibility screen. If any evidence is missing or requires verification, you must manually send the correspondence associated with the tasks based on the information required to process the application. Once all the verifications and issues or flags have been resolved, an application can be authorized. When you select Authorize , a potential eligibility check record is created on the application case. Viewing details of decisions The following screens can be used to view details of decisions for each criterion: Approved: Approval tab on Benefit line item can be expanded to view the criteria assessed. Closure: Closure tab on Benefit line item can be expanded to view the criteria assessed. Evidence: If an evidence issue exists, you can navigate to the evidence issue screen and view all the evidence which have an issue. Each individual evidence can be accessed to learn more about the issues. All client registered: If this criterion is not met, the user can check all the applicants on the application case to confirm which user is not registered. Identity confirmed: If this criterion is not met, the user can validate if there is outstanding verification on Name and SIN evidence. If there is a duplicate application during the authorization, the user will have to close one of them before authorizing the other. If the client is already receiving benefits, you will need to manually close the duplicate application. After the benefit has been authorized, the Old Age Security Integrated Case and Product Delivery Case are created. The Integrated Case will also be used for the GIS . If the client already has an Integrated Case or a Product Delivery Case, the cases will be updated with any new evidence information. Clients can receive OAS and GIS benefits together. However, they cannot receive ALW / ALWS Benefits along with OAS/ GIS . In some cases, an application may be added in Cúram and later denied. You must deny these applications in Cúram and the associated task should be closed. You can manually reopen a closed or withdrawn OAS or GIS benefit on the OAS GIS combined application case. This is possible when an Administrative Error , Appeal Decision , Request for Reconsideration, and/or a Response Received from SSA Country reopening reasons are met. Spouse and Non-Pensioner Spouse Non-Pensioner spouses are required to be registered as a Person to authorize GIS Benefit. Relevant tasks must be resolved. If there is a non-pensioner spouse on the application case, the benefit still needs to be authorized to close the application case. However, since the spouse is a non-pensioner, they will not be eligible for GIS . When an application is submitted with a spouse, you will need to deny their GIS benefit. If a spouse’s address differs from the primary applicant’s address, the provided address must be reviewed to ensure it matches the one listed on the application. In cases where the system has not automatically updated the spouse’s address, a manual update must be performed to reflect the correct address. GIS When a client qualifies for GIS , a single Old Age Security Benefit case is created and maintained to handle renewals on an annual basis. If the income is missing, it can be manually added. Active Application Details evidence with GIS must exist for the client before performing an override. If there are two applicants on a GIS application, both applicants must have Application Details evidence recorded. Failure to capture Application Details for both applicants will prevent the system from proceeding with GIS authorization. Marital Relationship The full period of the marital relationship must be provided to determine entitlement for income tested benefits. When a spouse’s date of death is added, the application case is automatically updated with this information, along with the marital status. If there is period of entitlement when the spouse was alive then you will add the spouse and their income to the application case. It is still possible to confirm a client’s marital status without requiring a date of marriage. You can contact the client to obtain the start date of the marriage. Ideally, the start date of the marriage should align with the start date of the benefit. If the marriage start date is provided within the same month as the benefit effective date, the benefit calculation can include the marital status from the benefit start date. When a person’s marital status is not aligned with the system’s record, Cúram will prevent the application from being processed. Marital status at the Person level cannot be updated directly. Instead, users must navigate to the application case and update the marital relationship evidence. Once the marital relationship evidence is activated, the marital status at the Person level will automatically update. Eligibility and Future Effective Date An application may have a future effective date, which can be found on the Client’s Application Case or their Integrated Case. The future effective date is located within the Application Details evidence under the Evidence tab. If all required criteria are met, a benefit can be authorized with a future effective date. On the eligibility check records, the user can view a detailed summary of all the criteria assessed to determine eligibility. Ensure correct application date is entered to ensure eligibility is properly calculated. The initial period of eligibility is determined based on the date of application, not the processing date. Eligibility for benefits is assessed from when the application was submitted. For Clients where earliest date of eligibility is more than 11 months after the application receipt date (For example, a 63-year-old Client submitting an OAS application), a user may add the "Initial Eligibility Period" Override to the case prior to authorization. This will not result in the Client meeting the Eligibility & Entitlement criteria earlier than under normal circumstances, but will allow for the application to be approved even if the calculated earliest date of eligibility is beyond the 11 months following the receipt date of the application. The initial eligibility period override does not extend the retroactive period for applications submitted after the earliest date of eligibility. The system will calculate retroactive benefits, including underpayments, automatically. When a client requests a retroactive payment or underpayment be issued immediately, you can issue the priority payment through the Issue Retro Pending Payments function in the product delivery case. Manual Payment and Priority Payment—Record and Issue in Cúram (Action) Documents During a triage task, the processor may be unsure about where to move the document. A document should be reviewed to determine where it should be moved to by the processing agent. If the document is related to or in support of an application, then it should be moved to the Application Case. If the document is about the individual and not specific to a benefit, then it can reside at the person level. The user needs to determine why the document was provided and then move it to the appropriate location to action. There will be cases that a document has to go to the Person (e.g. paper application received and there is no Application Case) and then the document can be moved afterwards if required. A document received for a verification cannot be moved from a Task directly to the verification. Documents for verifications must be moved to the location where the verification exists (e.g. Person) and then can be moved to the verification. This process applies to all document types, as there are no rules that prevent a user from moving a document type to a Case or a Person.

An Application Case is created when the client applies for an OAS pension and/or income-tested benefits (i.e. GIS, ALW and ALWS benefits) by submitting the application form either via paper or the client portal in Cúram. You can find an Application Case by clicking Applications on the page group navigation bar under the Cases and Applications tab of the Person Record. There are 2 types of Application Cases: OAS/GIS Application Case ALW / ALWS Application Case It is important to accurately record all details provided by the client as appropriate evidences, prior to authorizing an Application Case. You can verify the client's potential eligibility using the Check Eligibility function prior to authorization. When you initiate the authorization process, Cúram conducts an eligibility check as the first step. An Application Case can be authorized once all information is gathered. If the authorization is approved and successful, the client is eligible for a benefit and will have their entitlement determined. A correspondence letter will be sent out automatically through Cúram to inform the client. If the required information is not received, the application case must be closed and could result in the client not being eligible for or entitled to benefits. A correspondence letter will be sent out automatically through Cúram to inform the client of the decision as well. You can manually reopen a closed or withdrawn Application Case when the situation allows. For example, if the client requests reconsideration of a decision, and the Department changes the decision after processing the reconsideration or if the Department receives the agreement information from another country. Both the OAS pension and GIS applications can exist in one Application Case. If that is the case, Cúram requires separate authorization for each benefit. After the benefit authorization results in Approval, Cúram automatically creates the Integrated Case and Product Delivery Case to manage and deliver the benefit. If the Application Case has 2 benefits, Cúram still creates one Integrated Case and one Product Delivery Case after the first benefit is authorized and approved. This ensures these payments won't be included in any future entitlement calculations because the amount owing has been cleared.

When a domestic bank account is added or edited, Cúram automatically reviews the details and compares them against the Bank Account Fraud List. If the account information matches an entry on the fraud list, the validation check will fail, and the bank account evidence cannot be applied. In such cases, a task is automatically generated and sent for further review. This process does not impact the authorization of benefits. The client will still receive payment, which will be issued by cheque.

Cúram features workspace tabs that allows Integrity Services Branch (ISB) staff to manage the Bank Account Fraud List and Previously Compromised Client Account List, including adding, editing, and deleting entries. Additionally, Cúram automatically performs checks for both lists whenever a new or updated domestic bank account is entered. If the account information matches an entry on the Bank Account Fraud List, the validation check will fail and the bank account evidence cannot be applied. This process does not impact the authorization of benefits. The client will still receive payments which will be issued by cheque. If the account information matches an entry on the Previously Compromised Client Account List, the PREVIOUSLY COMPROMISED CLIENT ACCOUNT indicator will display on the person record. These accounts require additional authentication to complete transactions.

If you attempt to add a new bank account to Cúram and the bank account appears on the Bank Account Fraud List or Previously Compromised Client Account List, you will receive a warning message indicating that the bank account has been flagged as fraudulent or it is being added to a previously compromised client. The Bank Accounts evidence can only be saved in In Edit status and cannot be activated. Cúram will automatically generate a task for further review and the task will be assigned to a SCBO trained on how to review fraudulent bank accounts and previously compromised accounts.

A work queue is a central repository that organizes, holds, and tracks the tasks that need to be completed within the system. Work queues are used to manage and monitor user-created, or system-generated workload. There are two types of work queues: automatic work queues and manual work queues. Team members will only be subscribed to manual work queues. Team leads will be subscribed to both automatic and manual work queues to monitor workload, however, team leads will only subscribe team members to manual queues. Automatic work queues are used to hold tasks that can be automatically assigned by the system to users. Manual work queues are used to manage specific tasks that require manual intervention for allocation. A campaign work queue is a work queue created a result of an organization-planned activity or an event. It is organized with the purpose to complete an identified set of tasks by a specific group of staff members. Work queues have been configured specifically for OAS. In addition to automatic and manual work queue configurations, work queues are defined by region and purpose. Each region has a respective automatic and manual work queue Additionally, there are different work queues based on region (region or national), type of workload (migrated from legacy or generated in Cúram), and work queues by business units.

You can reissue a cancelled payment to the original or an alternative nominee. The reissued payment amount is calculated using the current active deductions at the time the payment is reissued. All reissued cancelled payments are paid on a daily payment schedule and will be picked up by the system on the next daily payment run. This will be done most often to reissue the payment to a different nominee (e.g. the payment went directly to the client but should have been issued to a third party) or can be used to correct incorrect deductions when the payments are NIL or under threshold and do not have non-reversible deductions. Cúram checks if the payment includes any of the following deductions towards: Interest (including liability offset amounts); Penalties (including liability offset amounts); OAS overpayments (including liability offset amounts); and CPP overpayments (cross program receivables) If any of these deductions are present, Cúram increases the Outstanding Balance Amount by the amount of the reversed deductions.

Recalculating gross to net amounts using current deductions and the current maximum deduction amounts This feature improves how the system handles deductions when it reissues a cancelled payment. What's changed When Cúram reissues a cancelled payment, it uses a new gross to net amount calculation. The existing controls still prevent double deductions for prior-year payments and ensures the system does not apply deductions when there is no outstanding balance. Why it matters As a result of this feature, Cúram applies the most current deductions and the current maximum deduction amount in effect at the time of reissue. It no longer reuses outdated deductions from the original payment. Benefits This feature offers the following benefits: Over collection or under-collection of departmental receivables is prevented. Processing staff no longer needs to manually deduct adjustments. Errors, rework, and audit risks are reduced. Clients receive the correct payment without delay. Payments are reissued faster and debt recovery is more reliable by aligning deductions with current account conditions. Overall, reissued payments now automatically apply current deduction rules, improving accuracy, efficiency, and financial integrity while reducing manual effort.

CPP and OAS clients accounts who are paid under International Agreements (IA) are processed and maintained in the IA legacy system. As part of the Benefits Delivery Modernization (BDM) project, the OAS-IA clients have been migrated to a new system called Cúram. As a result, a solution was required to continue to pay the CPP-IA clients. The decision was made to migrate the CPP-IA accounts into the CPP corporate system - ITRDS . Moving forward, to process CPP-IA benefits: CPP-IA data will need to be migrated from the IA legacy system to the ITRDS /Enterprise Database (EDB); The solution will produce operational reports to support the processing network as well as statistical reports for analysis purposes; CPMS will process the payments and incorporate them into its current solution to send the data to the Standard Payment System at Public Services and Procurement Canada; and The solution will exchange CPP-IA data with our internal and external partners, inbound and outbound. Effective March 10, 2025, approximately 20,000 CPP-IA client accounts will migrate to ITRDS and CPMS . The International Operations (IO) network recently received full training in processing and maintaining benefits through ITRDS and CPMS . The purpose of this implementation bulletin is to identify what has changed in ITRDS and CPMS for the remainder of the CPP network (CPP Processing, Call Centres, In-Person, and Integrity) at implementation.

The CPP-IA Migration of client accounts from the IA legacy system to ITRDS will result in ITRDS becoming the system of record for all CPP client accounts. All benefit processing and maintenance for CPP will be done in ITRDS . In addition, all monetary functions will be performed in CPMS . The IA legacy system will eventually be decommissioned. At this time: There will be no changes to CPP domestic screens in the legacy system.​ The 1I screens (2,3,4 and 5) will remain available, as they currently are, to all users who have access until a solution has been implemented in Cúram. ​ Once OAS Migration has been completed, the 1i5 screen will be disabled.

It clearly defines the file development process and explains when to resolve outstanding information gaps, noting that not all gaps impact the eligibility determination. It is essential that the decision to develop the file is relevant to ensure a fair and accurate outcome. In other words, the decision to develop the file is made on a case-by-case basis, based on the specific details of the applicant's situation and any identified missing information. In addition, file development documentation has been updated to support accurate recording.
